Concerning His words governing creation, He, exalted is He, says:

“And your Lord’s gracious word to the Children of Israel was fulfilled because of their patience.”

Another example is the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, widely transmitted from him through numerous chains in the collections of authentic hadith, Sunan, and Musnads. When seeking refuge, he would say:

“I seek refuge in Allah’s perfect words, beyond which neither the righteous nor the wicked can pass.”

It is well known that these are His words governing creation: nothing falls outside His will and His act of creation. As for His words in matters of religion, the wicked have contravened them by disobeying Him.

The point here is that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explained that the way is made easy for people to reach the final destinies of happiness or misery for which they were created, through the deeds that lead them there. The same applies to all other created things. He, glorified is He, creates children and other living creatures in wombs through His ordaining the mating of the two parents and the meeting of their two fluids in the womb. Thus, if someone were to say, “I put my trust in Allah and will not have intercourse with my wife, for if it has already been

---

## Page 4607

decreed that I should have a child, it will come into being; otherwise it will not, and there is no need for intercourse,” he would be a fool. This is unlike someone who has intercourse but withdraws before ejaculation, for withdrawal does not prevent a child from being conceived if Allah wills, since semen may escape involuntarily. An example of this is the report established in the two Sahīh collections from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said:

“We went out with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on the campaign against Banū al-Mustaliq and took some Arab captives. We desired women, found abstinence very difficult, and wished to practise withdrawal. We asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about this, and he said, ‘There is no harm in your not doing so, for Allah has already decreed whatever He will create until the Day of Resurrection.’”

In Sahīh Muslim, Jābir reported:

“A man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, ‘I have a slave woman who serves us and waters our date palms. I have intercourse with her, but I do not want her to become pregnant.’ He said, ‘Practise withdrawal with her if you wish, for whatever has been decreed for her will come to her.’”

All this is so even though Allah, glorified is He, is capable of what He has already done: creating a human being without either parent, as He created Adam; creating someone from a father alone, as He created Eve from Adam’s short rib; and creating someone from a mother alone, as He created the Messiah, son of Mary, peace be upon him. But He brought these creations into being through other, unusual causes.

Although this matter is denied only by heretics who set aside the revealed laws, many revered shaykhs have fallen into error over many of its subtleties: one of them lets himself drift along with the divine decree

---

## Page 4608

without duly upholding His commands and prohibitions, regarding this as entrusting his affairs to Allah, relying upon Him, and going along with the reality of divine decree. He imagines that the saying, “The servant should be with Allah like a corpse in the hands of the one washing it,” entails ceasing to observe commands and prohibitions. Thus he abandons what he has been commanded to do and does what he has been forbidden, until the light and discernment by which he distinguishes between what Allah has commanded, loved, and approved, and what He has forbidden, hated, and been displeased with, grow dim within him. He then treats as equal what Allah has distinguished, as the Most High says:

“Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their life and their death? Evil is their judgment!”

The Most High also says:

“Shall We then treat those who submit to Allah like the criminals? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?”

And the Most High says:

“Shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who spread corruption on earth? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked?”

And the Most High says:

“Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?”

And the Most High says:

“The blind and the seeing are not equal,”

“nor are darkness and light,”

“nor shade and scorching heat,”

“nor are the living and the dead equal. Indeed, Allah causes whom He wills to hear, but you cannot make those in the graves hear.”

There are many similar passages. Matters go so far with the extremists among them that they no longer distinguish between the command to carry out what Allah and His Prophet have prescribed in the revealed law, which distinguishes truth from falsehood—as set out in the Quran and Sunnah—and the states that occur in existence through unbelievers and the wicked. They perceive what unites all these things in that they all come about through Allah’s decree, predestination, lordship, and universal will

---

## Page 4609

and that all of it falls within His dominion. Yet they fail to perceive the distinction Allah has drawn between His allies and His enemies, the righteous and the wicked, believers and unbelievers, and the obedient who heed His religious command and the disobedient who defy it. To support this, they cite ambiguous statements transmitted from certain spiritual masters, or some of those masters’ errors.

This is a “momentous principle,” among the matters most deserving of attention from those who tread the path to Allah and follow the way of aspiration—the aspiration of those who seek His Face. Through neglecting it, some groups among them have fallen into unbelief, wickedness, and disobedience to an extent known only to Allah. They even become accomplices in oppression and aggression to unjust and arrogant men who wield power on earth. Such are those who direct their hearts toward assisting those they favor among the people who seek supremacy and spread corruption on earth, imagining that if they possess inward states through which they exert an influence in this regard, they are thereby among Allah’s allies.

For hearts exert a greater influence than bodies. If they are sound, their influence is sound; if they are corrupt, their influence is corrupt. Thus, the influence of these states is sometimes beloved to Allah and sometimes hateful to Him. The jurists have discussed the obligation to exact retribution by execution from someone who kills another by inward means, where such retribution is warranted.

In their inner selves and hearts, they appeal to the universal decree as evidence. They regard the mere occurrence of something beyond the ordinary for one of them—whether an unveiling granted to him or an influence that accords with his will—as an honor bestowed upon him by Allah. They do not realize that it is, in reality, a humiliation, that true honor lies in steadfast uprightness, and that

---

## Page 4610

Allah has bestowed no greater honor upon His servant than conformity to what He loves and is pleased with: obedience to Him and His Messenger, allegiance to His allies, and enmity toward His enemies. These are the allies of Allah of whom He says:

“Unquestionably, the allies of Allah will have no fear, nor will they grieve.”

If they conform to what He has made obligatory upon them, they are among those who follow the middle course. If they conform both to what He has made obligatory and to what He loves, they are among those brought near to Him—although everything obligatory is beloved to Him, not everything beloved to Him is obligatory.

As for the ease with which Allah tests His servant, whether through extraordinary occurrences or otherwise, or the adversity with which He tests him, this is not because the servant is honored or despised by his Lord. Rather, some may attain felicity through these trials if they obey Him in them, while others may come to misery through them if they disobey Him in them.

Allah Most High says:

“As for man, when his Lord tests him by honoring him and granting him blessings, he says, ‘My Lord has honored me.’

“But when He tests him by restricting his provision, he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me.’ No!”

Thus, with regard to these matters, people fall into “three categories”:

Those whose ranks are raised through extraordinary occurrences when they use them in obedience to Allah; those who expose themselves to Allah’s punishment when they use them in disobedience to Allah, such as Balaam and others; and those for whom they have the status of permissible things.

---

## Page 4611

The first category consists of the true believers who follow their Prophet, the foremost of Adam’s descendants. His extraordinary occurrences served only to provide proof by which he established Allah’s religion, or to meet a need that helped him obey Allah.

Because errors concerning this principle are so widespread, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade passively yielding to divine decree without striving to do what one has been commanded and what benefits one. Muslim narrated in his Sahīh from Abū Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said:

“The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is good in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek Allah’s help, and do not give in to helplessness. If something befalls you, do not say, ‘If only I had done such and such, this and that would have happened.’ Rather, say, ‘Allah decreed this and did as He willed,’ for ‘if only’ opens the door to Satan’s work.”

In Sunan Abī Dāwūd, it is related:

“Two men brought a dispute before the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and he ruled against one of them. The man against whom he ruled said, ‘Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’ The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, ‘Allah censures helpless inaction. Rather, you must be resourceful; then, if something overcomes you, say: Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’”

Thus, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded the believer to strive for what benefits him and to seek Allah’s help. This accords with the words of the Most High:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help,”

and His words:

“So worship Him and put your trust in Him.”

Striving for what benefits the servant means obeying and worshipping Allah, for obedience to Allah is what benefits him, and nothing benefits him more. Everything that helps one obey Allah is itself an act of obedience, even if it belongs to the category of permissible things.

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Saʿd in an authentic hadith:

“You will never

---

## Page 4612

spend anything seeking Allah’s countenance without thereby rising in rank and standing—even the morsel you place in your wife’s mouth.”

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) thus explained that Allah censures helpless inaction, which is the opposite of resourcefulness: neglecting what one is commanded to do. Such neglect is incompatible with the capacity that accompanies an act, although it is not incompatible with the prior capacity upon which commands and prohibitions are predicated. For the capacity that necessarily entails an act accompanies it and pertains only to the act it enables, as Allah Most High mentions in His words:

“They were unable to hear,”

and His words:

“And they were unable to hear.”

As for the capacity to which commands and prohibitions relate, it may or may not be accompanied by the act. Thus Allah Most High says:

“Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by those who are able to make their way there.”

And the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to ʿImrān ibn Husayn:

“Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; and if you cannot, then on your side.”

On this matter, people fall into “four categories.” Some attend to commands and prohibitions, worship and obedience, acknowledging the divinity of the Lord—glory be to Him—whom they have been commanded to worship. Yet they do not attend to divine decree and predestination, trust in Allah, and seeking His help. This is the condition of many who engage in religious learning and devotional practice. Despite their good intentions and their reverence for Allah’s sacred bounds and rites, they are often overcome by weakness, helplessness, and lack of support. For it is seeking Allah’s help, trusting in Him, taking refuge in Him, and supplicating to Him that strengthen the servant and make his affairs easier.

---

## Page 4613

For this reason, one of the early generations said:

“Whoever wishes to be the strongest of people should put his trust in Allah.”

In the two Sahīh collections, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr reports that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) is described in the Torah as follows:

“We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of glad tidings, a warner, and a safeguard for the unlettered. You are My servant and My messenger; I have named you ‘the one who trusts in Allah.’ He is neither harsh nor hard-hearted, nor does he raise his voice in the marketplaces. He does not repay evil with evil; rather, he repays evil with good, pardoning and forgiving. I will not take his soul until, through him, I have set the crooked religion straight and opened blind eyes, deaf ears, and closed hearts, through their saying: ‘There is no god but Allah.’”

For this reason, it is reported that the bearers of the Throne were only able to bear it by saying, “There is no might nor power except through Allah.” It is established in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said:

“These words are one of the treasures of Paradise.”

Allah Most High says:

“Whoever puts his trust in Allah, He will suffice him.”

And He Most High says:

“Those to whom people said, ‘The people have gathered against you, so fear them,’ but this only increased them in faith, and they said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.’”

Through to His words:

“So do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers.”

In Sahīh al-Bukhārī, Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him), commenting on the words, “And they said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs,’” said: “Abraham, Allah’s close friend, said these words when he was cast into the fire, and Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) said them when people told them, ‘The people have gathered against you.’”

And (a second category: those who recognize the lordship of the True One and their dependence on Him, and seek His help, yet do so according to their own desires and inward experiences, without regard for the reality of what He commands and forbids, what pleases or angers Him, and what He loves. This is the condition of many who profess spiritual poverty and many Sufis. For this reason, they often

---

## Page 4614

base their actions on spiritual states through which they exert influence in the world, without seeking what pleases the Lord and what He loves. They frequently err, imagining that disobeying Him is what pleases Him. They thus end up setting aside His commands and prohibitions, calling this “reality.” They imagine that they must follow this reality of divine decree without restraint, disregarding the religious reality of His commands, which encompasses what pleases the Lord, what He loves, and His commands and prohibitions, both outwardly and inwardly.

Such people are often deprived of their spiritual states and may revert to various forms of sin and wickedness. Indeed, many of them turn away from Islam altogether, for the good outcome belongs to those who fear Allah. Whoever does not observe the limits of Allah’s commands and prohibitions is not among the God-fearing. Thus, they fall into some of the same errors as the polytheists: sometimes adopting an innovation they imagine to be divinely prescribed, and sometimes invoking divine decree against His commands.

When Allah Most High mentioned the things for which He condemned the polytheists in Surahs al-An'ām and al-A'rāf, He mentioned the religious practices they had invented and made into prescribed law. As He Most High says:

“When they commit an indecency, they say, ‘We found our forefathers doing this, and Allah has commanded us to do it.’ Say, ‘Allah does not command indecency.’”

He condemned them for forbidding what Allah had not forbidden and prescribing what Allah had not prescribed. He also mentioned their appeal to divine decree in His words, Most High:

“Those who associated others with Allah said, ‘Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have worshipped anything besides Him, nor would we have forbidden anything without His command.’”

Similar passages occur in Surahs al-Nahl, Yā Sīn, and al-Zukhruf. These people bear a resemblance to the polytheists in both respects.

As for the third category—those who turn away from worshipping Allah and seeking His help—they are the worst of these categories.

---

## Page 4615

The fourth category is the praiseworthy one: those who have truly fulfilled the words:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help,”

and His words:

“So worship Him and put your trust in Him.”

They sought His help in obeying Him and acknowledged that He is their God, whom alone they may worship, through obedience to Him and His Messenger. They acknowledged that He is their Lord:

“They have no protector or intercessor besides Him.”

They also acknowledged the truths expressed in His words:

“Whatever mercy Allah grants to people, none can withhold; and whatever He withholds, none can release thereafter.”

“If Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it except Him; and if He intends good for you, none can repel His bounty.”

“Say, ‘Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended harm for me, could they remove His harm? Or if He intended mercy for me, could they withhold His mercy?’”

For this reason, a number of scholars have said: “Turning to causes constitutes associating partners with Allah, contrary to His oneness; denying that causes are causes is a deficiency in reason; and disregarding causes altogether undermines the revealed law.” The trust in Allah that is commanded brings together the requirements of monotheism, reason, and the revealed law.

It has thus become clear that anyone who considers trust in Allah to be one of the spiritual stations of ordinary followers of the path has made a grave error, even if he is a leading shaykh—such as the author of ‘Ilal al-Maqāmāt (The Defects of the Spiritual Stations), who is among the most eminent shaykhs, and from whom the author of Mahāsin al-Majālis (The Merits of Gatherings) adopted this view.

The weakness of the argument advanced by those who hold this view has also become clear: they suppose that trust in Allah serves only the interests of ordinary people and contributes nothing to attaining the intended goal. The same applies to those who regard supplication in this way. This is akin to regarding the commanded deeds in the same way—as in the case of someone whose preoccupation with trusting in Allah distracts him from what is required of him in the way of

---

## Page 4616

taking the means that constitute prescribed acts of worship and obedience. If this person errs by abandoning the prescribed means included in Allah’s words,

“So worship Him and put your trust in Him,”

his error resembles that of the former person in abandoning the prescribed trust in Allah included in His words,

“So worship Him and put your trust in Him.”

However, it should be said: whoever trusts in Allah and supplicates to Him to obtain permissible things is among ordinary people; if he does so to accomplish recommended and obligatory deeds, he is among the elect. Likewise, whoever supplicates to Him and trusts in Him to obtain forbidden things wrongs himself. Whoever turns away from trusting in Allah disobeys Allah and His Messenger; indeed, he falls outside the reality of faith. How, then, can this station belong to the elect? Allah Most High says:

“Moses said, ‘O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then put your trust in Him, if you are Muslims.’”

He Most High also says:

“If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who can help you after Him?”

And He Most High says:

“And in Allah let the believers put their trust.”

He Most High also says:

“Say, ‘Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended harm for me, could they remove His harm?’”

Further on, He says:

“Say, ‘Allah is sufficient for me. In Him those who trust should put their trust.’”

Allah has mentioned these words, “Allah is sufficient for me,” sometimes in connection with obtaining benefit and at other times with averting harm. The first occurs in His words:

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us from His bounty, and so will His Messenger,’”

to the end of the verse.

The second occurs in His words:

“Those to whom people said, ‘The people have gathered against you

---

## Page 4617

, so fear them.’ But this only increased them in faith, and they said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’” And in His words, Most High:

“But if they intend to deceive you, then Allah is sufficient for you. He is the One who strengthened you with His help.”

His words,

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us from His bounty, and so will His Messenger,’”

contain a command to be content and to put one’s trust in Allah. Contentment and trust in Allah stand on either side of what has been decreed: trust precedes its occurrence, while contentment follows it. Thus, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would say in prayer:

“O Allah, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, keep me alive so long as life is better for me, and cause me to die when death is better for me. O Allah, I ask You to grant me fear of You in private and in public. I ask You to enable me to speak the truth in anger and in contentment. I ask You for moderation in poverty and in wealth. I ask You for bliss that never ends, and joy that never ceases. O Allah, I ask You for contentment after Your decree, and I ask You for the comfort of life after death. I ask You for the delight of looking upon Your Face, and I ask You for longing to meet You, without harmful adversity or a trial that leads astray. O Allah, adorn us with the adornment of faith, and make us rightly guided guides.”

This was narrated by Ahmad and al-Nasā’ī from the hadith of ‘Ammār ibn Yāsir.

What exists before the decree, however, is a resolve to be content, not actual contentment. Thus, some spiritual masters would resolve to be content before affliction struck, but when it did, their resolve crumbled. Something similar happens with patience and other qualities, as Allah Most High says:

“You certainly wished for death before you encountered it. Now you have seen it with your own eyes.”

And He Most High says:

“O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?”

“It is greatly hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do.”

“Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks as though they were a building

---

## Page 4618

firmly joined together.”

This verse was revealed when they said, “If we knew which deeds were most beloved to Allah, we would perform them.” Allah, Glorified and Most High, then revealed the verse concerning fighting in His cause, and some were averse to it.

For this reason, it is disliked for a person to expose himself to trials by binding himself, through pledges, vows, or the like, to something the Lawgiver has not made obligatory upon him; by seeking a position of authority; or by entering a land where there is plague. Thus, it is established through several routes in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade making vows and said:

“It brings no good; it merely extracts something from the miser.”

It is also established in the two Sahīh collections that he said to ‘Abd al-Rahmān ibn Samura:

“Do not ask for authority. If you are given it because you asked, you will be left to bear it on your own; but if you are given it without asking, you will be helped in discharging it. If you swear an oath and then see that another course is better, do what is better and expiate your oath.”

It is also established in the two Sahīh collections that he said concerning plague:

“If you hear of it in a land, do not enter it. If it breaks out in a land while you are there, do not leave to flee from it.”

It is also established in the two Sahīh collections that he said:

“Do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being. But when you do meet them, remain steadfast, and know that Paradise lies beneath the shade of swords.”

These and similar teachings indicate that a person should not pursue what imposes certain obligations and prohibitions upon him, only to become reluctant to fulfil his commitments—as happens with many who make covenants with Allah concerning various matters. Most such people fall into the trial of breaking their covenants.

They also indicate that when a person is tested, he must be patient and steadfast, and must not become complacent, so that he may be among those men who possess certainty and fulfil their obligations. All of this necessarily requires

---

## Page 4619

patience. Hence, Muslims agree that patience is obligatory in fulfilling duties and avoiding prohibitions. This includes enduring afflictions without giving way to anguish, and restraining oneself from following personal desires in matters Allah has forbidden.

Allah mentions patience in His Book in more than ninety places, and links it with prayer in His words, Most High:

“Seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive.”

“Seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.”

And His words:

“Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night,”

through to His words:

“And be patient, for Allah does not allow the reward of those who do good to be lost.”

“So be patient with what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before sunrise and before sunset.”

“So be patient. Indeed, Allah’s promise is true. And seek forgiveness for your sin”—to the end of the verse.

He has made “leadership in religion” the fruit of patience and certainty, saying:

“And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs.”

The whole of religion consists of knowing the truth and acting upon it. Acting upon it necessarily requires patience; indeed, even seeking knowledge of it requires patience. As Mu‘ādh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“Devote yourselves to knowledge, for seeking it for Allah’s sake is worship; knowing it is reverent fear; researching it is striving in Allah’s cause; teaching it to those who do not know it is charity; and discussing it is glorification of Allah. Through it Allah is known and worshipped, and through it Allah is exalted and His oneness affirmed. Through knowledge Allah raises people, making them leaders and guides whom others follow and to whose judgment they defer.”

He thus regarded researching knowledge as a form of striving in Allah’s cause, and such striving necessarily requires patience. For this reason,

---

## Page 4620

Allah Most High says:

“By time,
indeed, mankind is in loss,
except those who believe, do righteous deeds, urge one another to the truth, and urge one another to patience.”

And He says:

“Remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, men of strength and insight.”

Beneficial knowledge is the foundation of guidance, while acting upon the truth is right conduct. The opposite of the former is misguidance, and the opposite of the latter is waywardness. Misguidance is acting without knowledge, while waywardness is following one’s desires.

Allah Most High says:

“By the star when it descends,
your companion has neither strayed nor erred.”

Guidance can therefore be attained only through knowledge, and right conduct only through patience. For this reason, ‘Alī said:

“Indeed, patience is to faith what the head is to the body—when the head is cut off, the body is left without it.” Then he raised his voice and said: “Indeed, whoever has no patience has no faith.”

As for “contentment,” the scholars and spiritual masters among the followers of Imam Ahmad and others have differed over whether contentment with the divine decree is obligatory or recommended. There are two views: according to the first, it is among the deeds of those who take a middle course; according to the second, it is among the deeds of those brought near to Allah. ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Azīz said: “Contentment is rare, but patience is the believer’s mainstay.”

It has been related that the Prophet, may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him, said to Ibn ‘Abbās:

“If you can act for Allah’s sake with contentment and certainty, then do so. But if you cannot, there is much good in patiently enduring what you dislike.”

---

## Page 4621

For this reason, the Quran praises those who are content, but does not make such contentment obligatory. This concerns contentment with the afflictions the Lord brings upon His servant, such as illness, poverty, and upheaval. Allah Most High says:

“Those who are patient in hardship and suffering, and in times of battle.”

And He says:

“Or do you think you will enter Paradise without experiencing the like of what befell those who passed away before you? Hardship and suffering afflicted them, and they were shaken.”

Hardship affects wealth, suffering affects the body, and upheaval affects the heart.

As for “contentment with what Allah has commanded,” its essential foundation is obligatory and is part of faith. As the Prophet, may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him, said in an authentic hadith:

“He has tasted the sweetness of faith who is content with Allah as his Lord, Islam as his religion, and Muhammad as his Prophet.”

It is also a consequence of love, as we shall explain, if Allah Most High wills. Allah Most High says:

“But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge over their disputes, then find within themselves no objection to your judgment and submit wholeheartedly.”

And He says:

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them and had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us’”—to the end of the verse.

And He says:

“That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked His good pleasure, so He rendered their deeds worthless.”

And He says:

“Nothing prevents their contributions from being accepted except that they disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger, come to prayer only reluctantly, and spend only unwillingly.”

An example of “the first type” is what Ahmad, al-Tirmidhī, and others narrated from Sa‘d, from the Prophet, may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him, who said:

“Part of the happiness of the son of Adam is his seeking guidance

---

## Page 4622

from Allah and his contentment with what Allah has allotted him. And part of the misery of the son of Adam is his failure to seek guidance from Allah and his discontent with what Allah allots him.”

As for “contentment with prohibited things”—disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience—most scholars say that contentment with them is not sanctioned, just as loving them is not sanctioned. For Allah, glorified is He, neither approves of them nor loves them, even though He has ordained and decreed them. As He, glorified is He, says:

“Allah does not love corruption.”

And He Most High says:

“He does not approve of disbelief for His servants.”

And He Most High says:

“He is with them when they plot by night to say what He does not approve of.”

Rather, He is displeased with them, as He Most High says:

“That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked His good pleasure, so He rendered their deeds worthless.”

A group of scholars said that one should be content with them insofar as they are attributed to Allah as His creation, and displeased with them insofar as they are attributed to the servant as acts he performs and acquires. This view does not contradict the preceding one; rather, both rest upon a single principle. He, glorified is He, has only decreed things for a wise purpose. In view of that purpose, they are loved and approved of, although in themselves they may be disliked and disapproved of.

For a single thing may combine two qualities: it is loved on account of one and disliked on account of the other. As stated in the authentic hadith:

“I do not hesitate over anything I am to do as I hesitate over taking the soul of My believing servant. He dislikes death, and I dislike causing him distress, yet he must undergo it.”

As for one who advocates contentment with the decree, which is Allah’s attribute and act, but not with what is decreed, which

---

## Page 4623

is what He brings into being, he thereby departs from the point of the discussion. For the discussion is not about contentment with the attributes and acts that subsist in the essence of the Lord Most High, but about contentment with what He brings into being. We have explained the related matters elsewhere.

Although contentment is an action of the heart, it finds its fullest expression in praise. Indeed, some have explained praise in terms of contentment. Hence the Quran and Sunnah teach praising Allah in every circumstance, for this entails contentment with His decree.

The hadith states:

“The first to be called to Paradise will be those who constantly praise Allah, praising Him in prosperity and adversity.”

It is reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace,

“would say when something pleasing came to him, ‘Praise be to Allah, through whose grace good deeds are brought to completion.’ When something displeasing came to him, he would say, ‘Praise be to Allah in every circumstance.’”

Imām Ahmad’s Musnad records from Abū Mūsā al-Ash'arī that the Prophet said:

“When a servant’s child is taken in death, Allah says to His angels, ‘Have you taken the soul of My servant’s child?’ They reply, ‘Yes.’ He says, ‘Have you taken his heart’s delight?’ They reply, ‘Yes.’ He says, ‘What did My servant say?’ They reply, ‘He praised You and affirmed that to Allah we belong and to Him we return.’ He says, ‘Build My servant a house in Paradise and name it the House of Praise.’”

Our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is the bearer of the Banner of Praise. His community are those who constantly praise Allah in prosperity and adversity.

Praising Allah in adversity is prompted by two considerations:

The first is the servant’s knowledge that Allah, glorified is He, deserves this praise and is entitled to it in His own right. For He has made excellent everything He created and has perfected everything. He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, the All-Aware, the Most Merciful.

---

## Page 4624

The second is his knowledge that Allah’s choice for His believing servant is better than the servant’s choice for himself. Muslim relates in his Sahīh, as do others, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“By Him in whose hand is my soul, Allah decrees nothing for the believer except that it is good for him. This applies to no one but the believer: if prosperity comes his way, he gives thanks, and that is good for him; if adversity befalls him, he remains patient, and that is good for him.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thus explained that every decree Allah ordains for a believer who patiently endures affliction and gives thanks in prosperity is good for him. The Most High says:

“Indeed, in that are signs for everyone steadfast in patience and grateful.”

He mentions these two qualities in four places in His Book. As for someone who neither patiently endures affliction nor gives thanks in prosperity, it does not necessarily follow that the decree is good for him. Hence, to anyone who questions how this applies to sins decreed for a believer, I give two answers.

The first is that this concerns only what befalls the servant, not what the servant does. This is like the words of the Most High:

“Whatever good befalls you is from Allah”—meaning prosperity—“and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself”—meaning adversity.

Likewise, the Most High says:

“We tested them with good and bad, so that they might return”—meaning prosperity and adversity—as the Most High says:

“We test you with evil and good as a trial.”

And the Most High says:

“If good befalls you, it grieves them; but if you are afflicted with

---

## Page 4625

adversity, they rejoice at it.” Thus, good and evil may refer to pleasant and harmful experiences, or to acts of obedience and sins.

(The second answer is that this applies to the believer who is steadfast in patience and grateful. Sins diminish faith, but when the servant repents, Allah loves him, and his rank may rise through repentance.

Some of the early generations said: “David was better after repentance than he had been before his sin.” Whoever is granted repentance is as Saʿīd ibn Jubayr described: “A servant may perform a good deed through which he enters the Fire, and a servant may commit a sin through which he enters Paradise.” This is because he performs a good deed, keeps it before his eyes, and becomes conceited about it; or he commits a sin, keeps it before his eyes, and seeks Allah’s forgiveness and repents to Him for it. It is authentically established that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Deeds are judged by how they end.”

When a believer commits a sin, its punishment may be averted from him through ten means: he repents and Allah accepts his repentance, for one who repents of a sin is like one who has no sin; or he seeks forgiveness and is forgiven; or he performs good deeds that erase it, for good deeds remove sins; or his fellow believers pray for him and seek forgiveness for him, during his life and after his death; or they gift him some of the reward of their deeds, through which Allah benefits him; or his Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, intercedes for him; or Allah Most High tries him with afflictions in this world that expiate his sin; or He tries him with a stunning shock in the intermediate state, thereby expiating his sin; or He subjects him to such terrors on the plains of the Resurrection as will expiate his sin; or the Most Merciful of the merciful has mercy on him.

---

## Page 4626

Whoever, then, misses out on these ten means has only himself to blame, as Allah Most High says in what His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, relates from Him:

“O My servants, it is only your deeds that I record for you and then recompense you for in full. Whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame no one but himself.”

If, then, the believer knows that the decree is good for him when he is steadfastly patient and grateful—or if he has asked Allah to choose what is best for him and knows that part of a person’s happiness lies in asking Allah to choose for him and being content with what Allah has allotted him—then he is content with what is good for him. In an authentic hadith, ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“Allah issues His decree: whoever is content will receive pleasure, and whoever is displeased will receive displeasure.”

This hadith thus concerns contentment and asking Allah to choose what is best: contentment comes after the decree, whereas asking Allah to choose comes before it. This is more complete than adversity accompanied by patience. Hence, contentment is mentioned in the former report and patience in the latter.

If the decree is good for him when accompanied by patience, how much more so when accompanied by contentment! For this reason, the hadith states:

“The truly afflicted person is the one deprived of reward.”

This occurs in the report narrated by al-Shāfiʿī in his Musnad:

“When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died, they heard someone saying: ‘O household of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace! In Allah there is consolation for every affliction, a replacement for all that perishes, and compensation for all that is lost. So place your trust in Allah and your hope in Him, for the truly afflicted person is the one deprived of reward.’”

For this reason, grief that is incompatible with contentment has never been commanded. Besides being of no benefit, it may even be harmful. Nevertheless, it is pardoned so long as it is not accompanied by anything Allah dislikes.

---

## Page 4627

However, weeping over the deceased out of compassion is good and recommended, and does not conflict with contentment—unlike weeping because of one’s own loss. This clarifies the meaning of the Prophet’s words, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he wept over the deceased and said:

“This is a mercy that Allah has placed in the hearts of His servants. Allah shows mercy only to those of His servants who are merciful.”

Such weeping is not like that of someone who weeps over his own loss rather than out of compassion for the deceased.

When al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyād’s son ʿAlī died, he laughed and said: “I saw that Allah had decreed this, so I wished to be content with what Allah had decreed.” His state was good compared with that of those who give way to anguish. Yet showing compassion for the deceased while remaining content with the decree and praising Allah Most High—as the Prophet did, may Allah bless him and grant him peace—is more perfect. As Allah Most High says:

“Then he is among those who believe and urge one another to patience and urge one another to compassion.”

Thus, He, glorified be He, mentions mutual encouragement to patience and compassion. People fall into “four categories”: some have patience accompanied by hardheartedness; some have compassion accompanied by anguish; and some combine hardheartedness with anguish. The praiseworthy believer, however, patiently endures whatever befalls him and shows compassion to others.

Some who have written on this subject have supposed that contentment with Allah follows from love for Him. This holds only according to the “first basis”: being content with Him because He intrinsically deserves it, while the servant sets aside all consideration of his own interests. It does not hold according to the “second basis”: being content because one knows that what has been decreed is good for oneself. Moreover, love is directed toward Him, whereas contentment concerns His decree. Nevertheless, in support of what this author and others like him have said, one might argue that love for Allah is of two kinds:

---

## Page 4628

love for Him for His own sake, and love for Him because of His beneficence. Likewise, praise of Him is of two kinds: praise that He intrinsically deserves, and praise for His beneficence toward His servant. The two kinds of contentment thus correspond to the two kinds of love.

As for being content with Him, His religion, and His Messenger, this belongs to love. Hence, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, spoke of tasting faith, just as he spoke, in connection with love, of experiencing the sweetness of faith. These two authentic hadiths provide the foundation for discussions of spiritual experience and taste grounded in faith and sanctioned by revelation, as opposed to those rooted in misguidance and innovation.

In Sahīh Muslim, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:

“He has tasted faith who is content with Allah as his Lord, Islam as his religion, and Muhammad as his Prophet.”

In the two Sahīh collections, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:

“There are three qualities through which whoever possesses them will experience the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than everything else; that he loves a person solely for Allah’s sake; and that he hates to return to disbelief, after Allah has saved him from it, as he hates to be thrown into the Fire.”

This will become clear through the discussion of love. We therefore say:

Section

Love for Allah—indeed, love for Allah and His Messenger—is among the greatest obligations of faith, its most important foundations, and its loftiest principles. Indeed, it is the basis of every deed of faith and religion, just as

---

## Page 4629

belief in Him is the basis of every utterance of faith and religion. Every movement in existence proceeds from love, whether praiseworthy or blameworthy, as we have explained at length in one of our major treatises, “The Principle of Love.” All deeds of faith and religion proceed only from praiseworthy love, whose foundation is love for Allah, glorified and exalted is He. A deed arising from love that Allah condemns cannot be righteous. Indeed, all deeds of faith and religion proceed only from love for Allah.

Allah Most High accepts only deeds done seeking His Face, as is established in an authentic report from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Allah Most High says: ‘I have no need of any partners. Whoever performs a deed in which he associates another with Me, I disavow it, and it belongs entirely to the one he associated with Me.’”

Also established in an authentic report is the hadith of:

“The three who will be the first with whom the Fire is kindled: the Quran reciter who acts for show, the fighter who acts for show, and the giver of charity who acts for show.”

Rather, sincere devotion to Allah alone is the religion besides which Allah accepts no other. It is the religion with which He sent the messengers, from the first to the last, which He revealed in all the scriptures, and upon which the leading scholars of the people of faith agree. This is the essence of the prophetic call and the axis around which the Quran revolves.

Allah Most High says:

“The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.”

“Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah with sincere devotion to Him alone.”

“Surely, sincere devotion is due to Allah alone.”

This theme pervades the surah, occupying most of it. For example, He says:

“Say: ‘I have been commanded to worship Allah with sincere devotion to Him alone.’”

“‘And I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit to Him.’”

And onward to His words:

---

## Page 4630

“Say: ‘It is Allah I worship, with sincere devotion to Him alone.’”

And onward to His words:

“Is Allah not sufficient for His servant? Yet they threaten you with those they worship besides Him.”

And onward to His words:

“Say: ‘Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intends harm for me, can they remove His harm?’”

And the rest of the verse. Then onward to His words:

“Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say: ‘Even though they possess nothing and have no understanding?’”

“Say: ‘All intercession belongs to Allah. His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned.’”

“When Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter recoil in aversion; but when those worshipped besides Him are mentioned, they rejoice.”

And onward to His words:

“Say: ‘Is it other than Allah that you command me to worship, you ignorant people?’”

And onward to His words:

“Rather, worship Allah and be among the grateful.”

Allah Most High also relates, in the account of Adam and Iblīs, that Iblīs said:

“By Your might, I will surely mislead them all,”

“Except Your chosen servants among them.”

Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, you have no authority over My servants, except those of the misguided who follow you.”

And He says:

“Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and put their trust in their Lord.”

“His authority extends only over those who take him as their patron and those who associate partners with Allah.”

Thus He makes clear that Satan’s authority and his power to mislead extend only to those who are not among His chosen servants. Hence He says in the account of Joseph:

“Thus it was, so that We might turn evil and indecency away from him. Indeed, he was one of Our chosen servants.”

Satan’s followers are the inhabitants of the Fire, as Allah Most High says:

“I will surely fill Hell with you and all those among them who follow you.”

He, glorified is He, has also said:

“Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives anything less than that for whomever He wills.”

This verse concerns those who have not repented. Hence He singled out associating partners with Him and placed a qualification on what

---

## Page 4631

is other than it by making its forgiveness subject to His will. He thus states that He does not forgive associating partners with Him for anyone who has not repented of it, but forgives anything less than that for whomever He wills.

As for His words:

“Say: ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of Allah’s mercy. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.’”

This concerns those who repent. Hence He speaks generally and without qualification. The context of the verse, together with the circumstances of its revelation, makes this clear.

He, glorified is He, has stated in several places that people, earlier and later, were commanded only to do this. One example is the surah that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited to Ubayy when Allah Most High commanded him to recite it specifically to him, to convey it to him and let him hear it. He says:

“Those who were given the Scripture did not become divided until after clear evidence had come to them.”

“And they were commanded only to worship Allah with sincere devotion to Him alone, upright in faith,”

and the rest of the verse. This is the true meaning of the declaration, “There is no god worthy of worship except Allah.”

With this He sent all the messengers. Allah Most High says:

“We never sent a messenger before you without revealing to him: ‘There is no god but Me, so worship Me.’”

And He says:

“Ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: did We appoint gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?”

And Allah Most High says:

“We certainly sent a messenger to every nation, saying: ‘Worship Allah and shun false gods.’”

All the messengers began their call with this foundation, as Noah, peace be upon him, said:

“Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him.”

Likewise, Hūd, Sālih and Shuʿayb, peace be upon them, and others—each said:

“Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him.”

Especially the greatest

---

## Page 4632

of the messengers—Abraham and Muhammad, peace be upon them both—each of whom Allah took as a close friend. Through them Allah clarified this foundation, strengthened them in upholding it, and spread it. Abraham is the leader of whom Allah said:

“Indeed, I will make you a leader for mankind.”

Prophethood, Scripture and messengers were placed among his descendants. Those endowed with this prophethood and messengership belong to his family, whom Allah blessed. He, glorified is He, said:

“And when Abraham said to his father and his people, ‘Indeed, I disavow whatever you worship, except the One who created me, for He will surely guide me.’ And he made this an enduring declaration among his descendants, so that they might return.”

This declaration is the declaration of sincere devotion to Allah alone: disavowing every object of worship except the Creator who brought us into being. As the man mentioned in Surah Yā Sīn said:

“Why should I not worship the One who created me, and to whom you will be returned? Should I take other gods besides Him? If the Most Merciful intends harm for me, their intercession will not benefit me at all, nor can they save me. Indeed, I would then be clearly astray.”

In His account of Abraham, Allah Most High, after explaining the error of taking a heavenly body as a lord to worship besides Allah, said:

“When it set, he said, ‘O my people, I disavow whatever you associate with Allah. Indeed, I have turned my face towards the One who created the heavens and the earth, inclining to Him alone, and I am not one of those who associate partners with Him.’”

Up to His words:

“Yet you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down to you no authority.”

Abraham, the close friend of Allah, peace be upon him, said:

“Have you considered what you have been worshipping—you and your forefathers? They are enemies to me, except the Lord of all worlds, who created me and guides me; who feeds me and gives me drink; and when I am ill, He heals me; and who will cause me to die and then bring me to life.”

And Allah Most High said:

“You have indeed had an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said

---

## Page 4633

to their people, ‘We disavow you and whatever you worship besides Allah. We reject you.’”—and so on in the verse.

Our Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is the one through whom Allah established the religion devoted exclusively to Him—the religion of monotheism—and subdued the polytheists, both those who had always been polytheists and those among the People of the Scriptures who disbelieved. As reported by Imam Ahmad and others, he said:

“I have been sent with the sword ahead of the Hour, so that Allah alone is worshipped, without any partner. My provision has been placed beneath the shade of my spear, and humiliation and abasement have been laid upon those who oppose my command. Whoever imitates a people is one of them.”

Some of the verses Allah revealed to him concerning monotheism have already been cited. Allah Most High also said:

“By those ranged in ranks,”

up to His words:

“Indeed, your God is One,”

and then:

“Indeed, whenever they were told, ‘There is no god but Allah,’ they grew arrogant and said, ‘Are we really to abandon our gods for a mad poet?’ Rather, he brought the truth and confirmed the messengers,”

up to His words:

“Those will have a known provision—fruits—and they will be honoured.”

Then come His accounts of the prophets concerning monotheism and devoting religion sincerely to Allah, up to His words:

“Glory be to Allah above what they attribute to Him, except for Allah’s chosen servants.”

Allah Most High also said:

“Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will find no helper for them—except those who repent, mend their ways, hold fast to Allah, and devote their religion sincerely to Allah. Those will be with the believers, and Allah will grant the believers a tremendous reward.”

In short, this foundation, in Surahs al-Anʿām, al-Aʿrāf and al-Nūr, and in the Tā Sīn Mīm group of surahs,

---

## Page 4634

the Hā Mīm and Alif Lām Rā groups, the Mufassal surahs, and other Meccan surahs, as well as passages in the Medinan surahs, is frequently and clearly stated. It is the foundation of all foundations and the bedrock of religion, expressed even in the two surahs al-Kāfirūn and al-Ikhlās:

“Say, ‘O disbelievers’”

and

“Say, ‘He is Allah, One.’”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite these two surahs in voluntary prayers, such as the two units of prayer after circumambulation and the Sunnah prayer of Fajr. Both encompass the affirmation of Allah’s oneness. “Say, ‘O disbelievers’” encompasses affirming Allah’s oneness in action and intent: devoting religion sincerely to Allah through one’s purpose and will. This is what the masters of Sufism generally discuss. As for the surah “Say, ‘He is Allah, One,’” it encompasses affirming Allah’s oneness in word and action, as authentically reported in the two Sahīh collections from Ā’ishah:

“A man used to recite ‘Say: He is Allah, One’ in his prayer. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Ask him why he does that.’ He replied, ‘Because it describes the Most Merciful, and I love to recite it.’ He said, ‘Tell him that Allah loves him.’”

This surah thus contains a description of Allah, glorified and exalted, that refutes both those who deny His attributes and those who liken Him to creation. This has made it the authoritative foundation for questions concerning the divine Essence, as we have explained at length elsewhere. We have also discussed the imams’ reliance upon it, together with its explanation of al-Ahad (the One) and al-Samad (the Self-Sufficient), as explained by the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the Companions and the Successors, and the evidence supporting that explanation. Here, however, our concern is “affirming Allah’s oneness in action,” which means devoting religion sincerely to Allah, although

---

## Page 4635

the two kinds are interconnected. No one among the Jahmiyyah, who deny Allah’s attributes, or those who liken Him to creation is free of some form of associating partners with Allah in practice. The very foundation of their position involves associating partners with Him and equating Allah with His creation or with nonexistent things. Thus, those who deny His attributes equate Him with nonexistent things through negative attributes that entail neither praise nor the affirmation of perfection. Or they equate Him with deficient existing beings through attributes of imperfection. Likewise, when they affirm attributes, they—and others like them who liken Him to creation—equate Him with created things in their essential realities. They may even worship these things, setting them as equals to their Lord, assigning rivals to Him, and equating created beings with the Lord of all worlds.

The Jews frequently equate the Creator with created beings and liken Him to them, even describing Allah as powerless, poor, miserly, and possessing other such imperfections from which He must be declared free, though they are attributes of His creation. The Christians frequently equate created beings with the Creator, even ascribing attributes of lordship and qualities of divinity to created beings and allowing for them what befits only the Creator. Glorified and exalted is He, far above what the wrongdoers say!

Allah, glorified and exalted, has commanded us to ask Him to guide us to the straight path: the path of those whom He has blessed—the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous—not those who have incurred wrath, nor those who have gone astray. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The Jews have incurred wrath, and the Christians have gone astray.”

Within this community are people who resemble both groups, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“You will surely follow the ways of those who came before you in every detail, even if

---

## Page 4636

they entered a lizard’s hole, you would enter it too.” They asked, “O Messenger of Allah, the Jews and the Christians?” He replied, “Who else?” This hadith is recorded in both Sahīh collections.

Since the foundation of religious practice is sincere devotion to Allah—seeking Him alone—what is sought for its own sake is loved for its own sake, and this is perfect love. Yet what is required is most often described as worship, as in His words:

“I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me.”

And His words:

“O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you.”

There are many similar passages. Worship encompasses love in its utmost perfection and humility in its utmost perfection. Someone who is loved but neither venerated nor humbled before is not an object of worship; nor is someone who is venerated but not loved. Hence the Most High says:

“Among people are those who take others as equals to Allah, loving them as they love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah.”

He, glorified is He, thus explains that although those who associate partners with their Lord and take others as equals to Allah love them as they love Allah, the believers love Allah more intensely than those people love Allah and their idols. This is because the believers know Allah better, and love follows knowledge. Moreover, the believers devote all their love to Allah alone, whereas those people direct some of their love to others, sharing their love between Him and the rivals they set up beside Him. Clearly, the former is more perfect.

The Most High says:

“Allah presents an example: a man belonging to quarrelling partners and a man belonging exclusively to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah! But most of them do not know.”

The term ‘love’ has a broad and general scope: a believer loves Allah and loves His messengers, His prophets, and His believing servants, even though this is part of loving Allah, and even though the love due to Allah

---

## Page 4637

is deserved by no one else. Hence love for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is expressed in terms of what is due exclusively to Him: worship, turning to Him in repentance, devoting oneself wholly to Him, and the like.

All these terms encompass love for Allah, glorified and exalted is He. Just as He has made clear that love for Him is the foundation of religion, He has also made clear that religion is perfected as this love is perfected, and diminished as it diminishes. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The foundation of the matter is Islam, its pillar is prayer, and its pinnacle is jihad in Allah’s cause.”

He thus stated that jihad is the pinnacle of deeds—the highest and noblest of them.

The Most High says:

And so on until His words: “a great reward.”

The scriptural texts concerning the virtues of jihad and those who undertake it are numerous. It has been established that it is the best voluntary deed a servant can perform. Jihad is evidence of perfect love.

The Most High says:

“Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, and your clan…”

And so on to the end of the verse.

The Most High also says, describing those who love Him and whom He loves:

“O you who believe, whoever among you turns back from his religion, Allah will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers and mighty against the disbelievers, striving in Allah’s cause and fearing no blame from anyone.”

He thus describes those whom He loves and who love Him as humble toward the believers and mighty against the disbelievers, striving in Allah’s cause and fearing no blame from anyone.

---

## Page 4638

For love necessarily entails jihad: the lover loves what his beloved loves and hates what his beloved hates. He is loyal to those to whom his beloved is loyal and hostile to those to whom his beloved is hostile. He is pleased with what pleases his beloved and angered by what angers him; he commands what his beloved commands and forbids what he forbids. In all this, he is in accord with him.

These are the people whose pleasure brings their Lord’s pleasure and whose anger brings His anger, for they are pleased only with what pleases Him and angered by what angers Him. Thus the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to Abū Bakr concerning a group that included Suhayb and Bilāl:

“Perhaps you have angered them. If you have angered them, you have indeed angered your Lord.”

Abū Bakr then said to them, “My brothers, have I angered you?” They replied, “No; may Allah forgive you, Abū Bakr.”

Abū Sufyān ibn Harb had passed by them, and they had said, “The swords have not exacted their due from Allah’s enemy.” Abū Bakr said to them, “Do you say this of the chief of Quraysh?” Abū Bakr mentioned this to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who gave him the response quoted above. Those men had spoken only out of anger for Allah’s sake, owing to their complete loyalty to Allah and His Messenger and their enmity toward the enemies of Allah and His Messenger.

Hence the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in the authentic hadith he related from his Lord:

“My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. Through Me he hears, through Me he sees, through Me he strikes, and through Me he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him, and if he seeks My protection, I will surely protect him. I have never hesitated over anything I am to do as I hesitate over taking the soul of My believing servant: he dislikes death, and I dislike causing him distress, yet he must undergo it.”

He, glorified is He, thus explains that He hesitates, for hesitation is a conflict between two wills. He, glorified is He, loves what His servant loves

---

## Page 4639

and dislikes what he dislikes. His servant dislikes death, so He dislikes it, as He said, “I dislike causing him distress.” Yet He, glorified is He, has decreed death and therefore wills that His servant should die. He called this hesitation, then explained that it must nevertheless occur.

This is agreement and unity regarding what is loved, approved and commanded, and what is hated, disliked and forbidden. It may be called unity in kind and attribute, but it is not a union of the two essences. Such a union is utterly impossible, and whoever professes it is an unbeliever. This is the doctrine of the Christians and the extremists among the Rāfidah and the ascetics, such as the followers of al-Hallāj and their like. It is “restricted union,” concerning one particular entity.

As for “unrestricted union,” the doctrine of those who profess the unity of existence and claim that the existence of creation is the very existence of the Creator, this amounts to negating and denying the Maker and encompasses every form of polytheism.

Just as union is of two kinds, so too is indwelling. Some profess restricted indwelling in certain individuals; others profess His indwelling in everything. The latter are the Jahmiyyah, who say that Allah’s essence is everywhere.

Some of those overwhelmed by self-effacement in love may become so absorbed in their beloved that they lose awareness of themselves and their love; in the one they remember, of their remembrance; in the one they know, of their knowledge; and in the one they find, of their own existence. They perceive only their beloved and, in their loss of discernment, impaired reason and intoxication, imagine that they are their beloved.

It is related that a beloved fell into the sea, and his lover threw himself in after him. The beloved said:

---

## Page 4640

“I fell in, but what made you fall in?” He replied, “I was so absorbed in you that I lost awareness of myself and thought that you were me.”

There is no doubt that this is error and misguidance. But if it results from the intensity of love and remembrance, without any prohibited cause bringing about his loss of reason, then he is excused for that loss. He is therefore not held accountable for what he says in this state, in which he has lost his reason without a prohibited cause.

As has been said of the sane among the insane:

“They are people whom Allah granted reason and spiritual states. Then He took away their reason but left their spiritual states, and lifted the obligations He had imposed because of what He had taken away.”

If, however, the cause of his loss of reason is prohibited, the intoxicated person is not excused, although, according to the sounder of the two views, he is not judged an unbeliever. Likewise, according to the sounder of the two views, his divorce does not take effect, although the disagreement over this ruling is well known. We have discussed this at length, as well as whose spiritual state may be accepted and whose may not, in a “treatise” on the subject.

In any case, the self-effacement that leads a person to such a condition is an imperfect state, even if he is not legally accountable. For this reason, nothing of this kind has been reported from the Companions, who are the best of this community, nor from our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who is the best of the messengers—although those who experience such states find some basis for their position in Moses’ falling unconscious. Loss of reason upon receiving spiritual influxes from Allah occurred only among some of the Successors and those who came after them.

If perfect love entails agreement with the beloved in what he loves and hates, and in his friendships and enmities, then it is clear that whoever

---

## Page 4641

loves Allah with the love that is obligatory must hate His enemies and love what He loves, including waging jihad against them. As He, Most High, says:

“Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks as though they were a solid structure.”

One whose love is complete is unaffected by blame or reproach; rather, it encourages him to remain steadfast in his love, as so many poets have said. These are those who incur blame for praiseworthy reasons: they do not fear anyone who blames them for doing what Allah loves and is pleased with—waging jihad against His enemies. Indeed, blame for this is plentiful. But blame for doing what Allah dislikes or abandoning what He loves is justified. Patiently enduring such blame is not praiseworthy; rather, returning to the truth is better than persisting in falsehood. This makes clear the distinction between the “Malāmiyya” (people of blame) who do what Allah and His Messenger love, fearing no one’s blame for it, and the “Malāmiyya” who do what Allah and His Messenger hate and patiently endure blame for it.

Section

Since love is the foundation of every religious deed, fear, hope, and other such states necessarily entail love and have their basis in it. For someone who hopes and yearns only yearns for what he loves, not what he hates. And someone who fears flees from what he fears in order to attain what he loves.

He, Most High, says:

“Those whom they call upon

---

## Page 4642

seek a means of drawing near to their Lord, striving to be closest to Him, and hope for His mercy and fear His punishment”—to the end of the verse. He also says:

“Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in Allah’s cause—it is they who hope for Allah’s mercy.”

“His mercy” encompasses every good, and “His punishment” encompasses every evil. The abode of unalloyed mercy is Paradise, and the abode of unalloyed punishment is Hell. This world, however, is an abode in which the two are mingled.

Even when hope is directed toward entering Paradise, Paradise encompasses every delight, the highest of which is gazing upon the Face of Allah. Thus, in Sahīh Muslim, ʿAbd al-Rahmān ibn Abī Laylā relates from Suhayb that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, a caller will proclaim, ‘People of Paradise! Allah has made you a promise that He wishes to fulfil for you.’ They will say, ‘What is it? Has He not brightened our faces, made our scales heavy, admitted us to Paradise, and saved us from the Fire?’ Then,” he said, “the veil will be lifted, and they will gaze upon Him. Nothing He has given them will be dearer to them than gazing upon Him.”

This is the “additional reward.”

This dispels the confusion surrounding the statement of someone who says, “I have not worshipped You out of longing for Your Paradise or fear of Your Fire; rather, I have worshipped You out of longing to see You.” This speaker and those who follow him assumed that Paradise comprises nothing but eating, drinking, clothing, sexual relations, auditory pleasures, and similar enjoyment of created things. Those Jahmiyya who deny that Allah will be seen agree with him on this, as do those who acknowledge that He will be seen but claim that there is no enjoyment in seeing Allah itself—a view held by some who study jurisprudence. Thus, they all agree that what is meant by Paradise and the Hereafter

---

## Page 4643

includes nothing but the enjoyment of created things. Thus, one of the mistaken shaykhs, upon hearing His words:

said, “Where, then, are those who desire Allah?” Another, commenting on the words of the Most High:

said, “If lives and wealth are exchanged for Paradise, where does gazing upon Him come in?” All this stems from their assumption that Paradise does not include gazing upon Him.

The “correct understanding” is that Paradise is the abode encompassing every delight, the highest of which is gazing upon the Face of Allah. This is among the delights they will attain in Paradise, as the revealed texts inform us. Likewise, the people of the Fire enter it veiled from their Lord.

Nevertheless, if the person making such a statement understands what he is saying, he means only: “Even if You had not created a Fire, or had not created a Paradise, it would still be obligatory to worship You, draw near to You, and gaze upon You.” By Paradise here, he means the pleasures enjoyed by created beings.

As for a living being acting without any love or will whatsoever, this is impossible, although some mistaken ascetics imagine it and suppose that a servant’s perfection consists in having no will whatsoever. Such a person speaks while in a state of fanā (self-effacement). The person in that state—absorbed in his beloved—does have will and love, but is unaware of them. The existence of love is one thing, will another, and awareness of it yet another. Because they were unaware of it, they supposed it did not exist. This is a mistake: it is inconceivable that a servant should ever act except from love, aversion, and will. Hence the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The truest names are Hārith and Hammām.”

Every person thus has a pursuit, namely, his work, and an intention, which is the basis of

## Page 4644

will. Yet at times the heart holds such love for Allah as prompts a person to obey Him, and such reverence for Him and shame before Him as restrains him from disobeying Him. As ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: “What an excellent servant Suhayb is! Even if he did not fear Allah, he would not disobey Him.” That is, he would not disobey Him even without fearing Him—so how much more so when he does fear Him! His reverence and honour for Allah prevent him from disobeying Him.

When a person’s fear and hope concern the torment of his Lord veiling Himself from him and the delight of His revealing Himself to him, these clearly follow from his love for Him. Love is what gives rise to the longing for Him to reveal Himself and the fear of His veiling Himself. If, instead, his fear and hope concern suffering or enjoyment through created things, he seeks this only through worshipping Allah, which necessarily entails loving Him. Then, when he experiences the sweetness of loving Allah, he finds it sweeter than every other love. Hence, the people of Paradise are occupied with this above all else, as stated in the hadith:

“The people of Paradise will be inspired to glorify Allah just as they are inspired to breathe.”

This shows the supreme delight they take in remembering Allah and loving Him. Thus, fear of suffering through created things and hope of enjoyment through them lead a person to love Allah, which is the foundation.

All of this rests upon “the foundation of love.” We therefore say: the Book and the Sunnah explicitly mention the love of the believing servants, as in His words:

the end of their term. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.”

The deeds Allah loves—obligatory and recommended, outward and inward—are many and well known. Likewise, His love for those who perform them is well known: they are the believers, the pious allies of Allah. This love is real, as declared by the Quran and Sunnah. The position of the early generations of this community and its imams, the people of the Sunnah and hadith, all the religious teachers whose example is followed, and the imams of Sufism is that Allah, glory be to Him, is loved for His own sake with genuine love. Indeed, this is the most perfect love, as He, exalted is He, says:

“But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah.”

Likewise, He, glory be to Him, genuinely loves His believing servants. The Jahmiyyah denied the reality of love on both sides, claiming that love requires an affinity between the lover and the beloved, and that there is no affinity between the eternal and the created that would give rise to love. The first to introduce this innovation into Islam was al-Jaʿd ibn Dirham, early in the second century AH. Khālid ibn Abd Allāh al-Qasrī, the governor of Iraq and the East, slaughtered him as a sacrifice at Wāsit.

He addressed the people on the Day of Sacrifice, saying:

“O people, offer your sacrifices! May Allah accept your sacrifices. I shall sacrifice al-Jaʿd ibn Dirham, for he claimed that Allah did not take Abraham as a close friend, nor did He speak to

## Page 4647

Moses directly.” Then he stepped down and slaughtered him.

Al-Jahm ibn Safwān had adopted this doctrine from him, proclaimed it openly, and argued in its defence. The Jahmiyyah doctrine was named after him. Salm ibn Ahwaz, the governor of Khurāsān, then killed him there. This doctrine subsequently passed to the Muʿtazilah, the followers of ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd. Their views gained prominence during the caliphate of al-Maʾmūn, until the imams of Islam were subjected to an inquisition and called upon to agree with them on this.

This doctrine of theirs was originally derived from the polytheists and Sabians among the Brahmins, the philosophers, and the innovators among the People of the Book, who claim that the Lord has no positive attributes whatsoever. You have permeated the pathways of my soul;
Thus a close friend bears the name khalīl.

This is supported by the report established in the Sahīh from Abū Saʿīd, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

In another version: “Allah has taken me as a close friend, just as He took Abraham
