Thus, the whole of religion falls within worship. An authentic report states:

“When Gabriel came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the form of a Bedouin and asked him about Islam, he replied, ‘It is to testify that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah and that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger, to establish prayer, to give zakah, to fast Ramadan, and to perform pilgrimage to the House if you are able to make the journey.’

“He asked, ‘What, then, is faith?’ He replied, ‘It is to believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, resurrection after death, and divine decree, both its good and its evil.’

“He asked, ‘What, then, is excellence in worship?’ He replied, ‘It is to worship Allah as though you see Him; and though you do not see Him, He certainly sees you.’ Then, at the end of the hadith, he said, ‘This was Gabriel, who came to teach you your religion.’”

He thus included all of this within religion. The word dīn (religion) encompasses submission and humility. One says, Dintuhu fa-dāna, meaning, “I humbled him, and he became humble.” Likewise, yadīnu Allāha and yadīnu lillāh mean that a person worships Allah, obeys Him and submits to Him. Thus, Allah’s religion consists of worshipping Him, obeying Him and submitting to Him.

---

## Page 4733

And the basic meaning of “worship” is likewise humility. A path is called mu‘abbad (well-trodden) when it has been worn smooth underfoot. Yet the worship that is commanded encompasses both humility and love: it entails the utmost humility before Allah together with the utmost love for Him. The final degree of love is “consummation.” Its first degree is “attachment,” because the heart becomes attached to the beloved; then comes “yearning,” because the heart pours itself towards the beloved; then “abiding love,” which remains firmly in the heart; then “passionate love”; and finally “consummation.” The expression Taym Allāh means “Allah’s servant”; thus, one utterly enamoured is enslaved to his beloved.

Whoever submits to someone while hating him is not worshipping him. Likewise, someone who loves something without submitting to it is not worshipping it, as with the love one may have for one’s child or friend. Hence, neither love nor humility alone suffices in worshipping Allah Most High. Rather, Allah must be dearer to His servant than everything else, and greater in his estimation than everything else. Indeed, none but Allah deserves perfect love and utter humility. Whatever is loved for other than Allah’s sake is loved in a corrupt manner, and whatever is venerated without Allah’s command is venerated falsely.

Allah Most High says:

“Say, ‘If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your clan, wealth you have acquired, trade whose decline you fear, and homes you cherish are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until Allah brings about His command.’”

Love, in its general sense, may therefore be directed to Allah and His Messenger, as may obedience; for obedience is due to Allah and His Messenger

---

## Page 4734

and Allah and His Messenger are to be pleased:

“Allah and His Messenger have a greater right that they should seek His pleasure.”

Giving, too, is attributed to Allah and His Messenger:

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them.”

As for “worship” and related acts, such as reliance, fear, and the like, these are for Allah alone, as He Most High says:

“Say, ‘O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is common between us and you: that we worship none but Allah and associate nothing with Him’”—up to His words: “But if they turn away, then say, ‘Bear witness that we are Muslims.’”

He Most High also says:

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them and had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger. To Allah alone we turn with longing.’”

Thus, giving is attributed to Allah and the Messenger, as in His words:

“Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it.”

As for sufficiency, it is Allah alone who suffices, as He Most High says:

“Those to whom people said, ‘The people have gathered against you, so fear them,’ but this only increased them in faith, and they said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’”

He Most High also says:

“O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for those believers who follow you.”

That is, Allah is sufficient for you and sufficient for those who follow you. Whoever supposes that the meaning is, “Allah, together with the believers, is sufficient for you,” has made a grave error, as we have explained at length elsewhere. He Most High also says:

“Is Allah not sufficient for His servant?”

To explain this precisely: the word “servant” may mean “one brought into subjection”—one whom Allah has subjected and humbled, and whose affairs He has governed

---

## Page 4735

and whose course He has directed. In this sense, all created beings are Allah’s servants: the righteous and the wicked, the believers and the disbelievers, and the people of Paradise and the people of Hell. For He is the Lord and Sovereign of them all. They cannot escape His will, His power, or His perfect words, which neither the righteous nor the wicked can overstep. Whatever He wills comes to pass, even if they do not will it; and whatever they will, if He does not will it, does not come to pass. As He Most High says:

“Do they seek a religion other than Allah’s, when all those in the heavens and the earth have submitted to Him, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned?”

He, glorified is He, is the Lord of all worlds, their Creator and Provider, the One who gives them life and causes them to die, turns their hearts, and directs their affairs. They have no Lord but Him, no Owner besides Him, and no Creator except Him, whether they acknowledge this or deny it, and whether they know it or are ignorant of it. The believers among them, however, know and acknowledge this, unlike those who are ignorant of it, or who deny it and arrogantly defy their Lord, neither acknowledging nor submitting to Him, despite knowing that Allah is their Lord and Creator.

Knowledge of the truth, when accompanied by an arrogant refusal to accept it and by denial of it, becomes a source of torment for the one who possesses it. As He Most High says:

“They denied them, though their souls were certain of them, out of injustice and arrogance. So see what was the end of those who spread corruption.”

He Most High also says:

“Those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize him as they recognize their own sons. Yet a group of them knowingly conceal the truth.”

He Most High also says:

“It is not you they disbelieve; rather, it is Allah’s signs that the wrongdoers reject.”

---

## Page 4736

Thus, if a servant acknowledges that Allah is his Lord and Creator, and that he is dependent upon Him and in need of Him, he understands servitude as it relates to Allah’s lordship. This servant asks his Lord, humbly implores Him, and relies upon Him. Yet he may obey His command or disobey it; despite this acknowledgment, he may worship Him, or he may worship Satan and idols. Such servitude does not distinguish the people of Paradise from the people of Hell, nor does it make a person a believer. As He Most High says:

“Most of them do not believe in Allah without associating partners with Him.”

The polytheists acknowledged that Allah was their Creator and Provider, yet they worshipped others besides Him. He Most High says:

“If you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, ‘Allah.’”

He Most High also says:

“Say, ‘To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you know?’ They will say, ‘To Allah.’ Say, ‘Will you not then take heed?’”

And so on, until His words:

“Say, ‘How, then, are you deluded?’”

Many of those who speak of reality and witness it are witnessing this reality, namely the “reality of the created order.” Believers and disbelievers, the righteous and the wicked, alike share in this reality, in witnessing it, and in knowing it. Iblīs acknowledges this reality, as do the people of Hell. Iblīs said:

“My Lord, then grant me respite until the Day they are resurrected.”

He also said:

“My Lord, because You have led me astray, I will surely make evil appealing to them on earth, and I will surely lead them all astray.”

And he said:

“By Your might, I will surely lead them all astray.”

And he said:

“Do You see this one whom You have honoured above me?”

He made other such statements in which he acknowledged that Allah was his Lord and Creator, and the Creator of others. Likewise, the people of Hell said:

“Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were

---

## Page 4737

a people astray.” And He Most High says:

“If only you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord! He will say, ‘Is this not the truth?’ They will say, ‘Yes, by our Lord!’”

Whoever stops at this reality and the witnessing of it, without fulfilling the religious reality he has been commanded to uphold—namely, worshipping Allah in recognition of His divinity and obeying His command and the command of His Messenger—is of the same kind as Iblīs and the people of Hell. If, moreover, he imagines himself to be among the elect of Allah’s allies and the people of spiritual knowledge and realization, for whom the divinely prescribed commands and prohibitions no longer apply, then he is among the worst people of disbelief and deviation.

Whoever supposes that al-Khidr and others were exempted from the divine command because they witnessed the divine will, or for similar reasons, has made one of the worst statements uttered by those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger.

Only when he enters into the “second sense” of “servant”—a servant in the sense of a worshipper—does he become a worshipper of Allah who worships none but Him. He then obeys His command and the command of His messengers, allies himself with His believing, God-fearing allies, and opposes His enemies. This worship pertains to His divinity. Hence the defining declaration of monotheism is: “There is no god but Allah.” This is unlike the state of someone who acknowledges His lordship but does not worship Him, or worships another god alongside Him.

A god is that which the heart worships with complete love, reverence, veneration, honour, fear, hope, and the like. This is the worship that Allah loves and is pleased with, by which He has described His chosen servants, and with which He sent His messengers.

As for “servant” in the sense of one subjected to servitude, whether he acknowledges this or denies it, that is a condition shared

---

## Page 4738

by believer and disbeliever alike. Distinguishing between these two kinds makes clear the distinction between “religious realities”—which belong to the worship of Allah, His religion, and His legislative command, which He loves and is pleased with, and whose adherents He takes as allies and honours with His Paradise—and “cosmic realities,” which believers and disbelievers, the righteous and the wicked, all share. Whoever contents himself with the latter without following the religious realities is among the followers of the accursed Iblīs and those who disbelieve in the Lord of all worlds. Whoever contents himself with them in some matters but not others, or at a particular spiritual station or in a particular state, suffers a diminution in his faith and his standing as an ally of Allah in proportion to his neglect of the religious realities.

This is a matter of immense importance in which many have erred and which has caused great confusion among those travelling the spiritual path. Indeed, so many eminent shaykhs claiming spiritual realization, monotheism, and spiritual knowledge have slipped here that none can count them except Allah, who knows what is concealed and what is made public.

Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir—may Allah have mercy on him—pointed to this in what has been related from him. He explained:

“Many men, when they reach the matter of divine decree and predestination, hold back. But not I: an opening was made for me in this matter, so I contended with the decrees of the Truth, through the Truth and for the Truth. A true man is one who contends with destiny, not one who simply goes along with it.”

What the shaykh—may Allah have mercy on him—described is precisely what Allah and His Messenger commanded. Yet many men have erred: they may witness the acts of disobedience and sins decreed for one of them, or such things decreed for people generally—even disbelief—and witness that all this occurs by Allah’s will, decree, and predestination, falls under the governance of His lordship, and follows from His will

## Page 4739

and so they regard submission to this, conformity with it, acceptance of it, and the like as religion, a spiritual path, and worship. Thus they resemble the polytheists who said:

They also said:

“No calamity befalls except by Allah’s permission. And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart.”

One of the early Muslims said: “This is a man whom calamity strikes, who knows that it is from Allah and so is content and submits.” Allah Most High also says:

“So that you neither grieve over what you have missed nor exult over what He has given you.”

In the two Sahīh collections, it is reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Adam and Moses disputed. Moses said, ‘You are Adam, whom Allah created with His hand, into whom He breathed of His spirit, before whom He made His angels prostrate, and whom He taught the names of all things. Why, then, did you bring us and yourself out of Paradise?’

“Adam said, ‘You are Moses, whom Allah chose to bear His message and to whom He spoke. Did you find that this had been written concerning me before I was created?’

“He replied, ‘Yes.’”

---

## Page 4740

Adam, peace be upon him, did not appeal to divine decree in his argument with Moses on the assumption that a sinner may plead divine decree as an excuse. No Muslim or rational person would say this. Were it an excuse, it would also excuse Satan, the people of Noah, the people of Hūd, and every disbeliever. Nor did Moses blame Adam for the sin itself, for Adam had repented to his Lord, who then chose him and guided him. Rather, he blamed him for the calamity that had befallen them because of that sin. This is why he said, “Why, then, did you bring us and yourself out of Paradise?” Adam answered that this had been written before he was created. Thus, both the deed and the calamity resulting from it had been decreed. One must submit to whatever calamities have been decreed, for this is part of being fully content with Allah as one’s Lord.

As for sins, Allah’s servant has no right to commit them. If he does sin, he must seek forgiveness and repent. Thus, he repents of his faults and patiently endures calamities. Allah Most High says:

“So be patient. Surely Allah’s promise is true. And seek forgiveness for your sin.”

Allah Most High also says:

“If you are patient and mindful of Allah, their schemes will not harm you at all.”

And He says:

“If you are patient and mindful of Allah, that is indeed a matter requiring firm resolve.”

Joseph said:

“Indeed, whoever is mindful of Allah and patient—Allah never lets the reward of those who do good go to waste.”

Likewise, regarding the sins of others, a person must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong—to the best of his ability—strive in Allah’s cause against the disbelievers and hypocrites, be loyal to Allah’s allies and oppose Allah’s enemies, and love for Allah’s sake and hate for Allah’s sake. As Allah Most High says:

“O you who believe, do not take My enemies and your enemies

---

Allah Most High also says:

“You will not find people who believe in Allah and the Last Day showing affection to those who oppose Allah and His Messenger.”

---

## Page 4742

disobey, between the righteous and the wicked, between the rightly guided and the misguided, between those given to perversity and those of sound judgment, and between the truthful and the liars.

Whoever witnesses “cosmic reality” without witnessing “religious reality” treats as equal these different categories between which Allah has drawn the clearest distinctions. Eventually, he comes to equate Allah with idols, as Allah Most High relates their words:

“By Allah, we were clearly astray”

“when we made you equal to the Lord of all worlds.”

Indeed, these people have gone so far as to equate Allah with everything that exists, making the worship and obedience due to Him a right belonging to everything that exists, since they identify Him with the very existence of created beings. This is among the gravest forms of disbelief and heresy concerning the Lord of all servants.

Their disbelief takes them so far that they no longer perceive themselves as servants—neither as those subjected to His dominion nor as those who worship Him. Rather, they perceive themselves as the Real, as their leading transgressors have explicitly stated, including Ibn ‘Arabī, author of al-Fusūs, and other heretical fabricators such as Ibn Sab‘īn and his like. They perceive themselves as both the worshippers and the worshipped.

This is not the witnessing of any reality, whether cosmic or religious. Rather, it is misguidance and blindness to cosmic reality: they identify the Creator’s existence with that of creation and attribute every blameworthy and praiseworthy quality to both Creator and creation, since, according to them, the existence of the one is the very existence of the other.

---

## Page 4743

As for those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, ordinary and distinguished alike, they are the people of the Book, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah has people of His own among mankind.” He was asked, “Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?” He replied, “The people of the Quran: they are Allah’s own people and His chosen ones.”

These believers know that Allah is the Lord, Sovereign, and Creator of everything, and that the Creator, glorified be He, is distinct from creation: He neither dwells within it nor is united with it, nor is His existence identical to its existence. Allah declared the Christians disbelievers for affirming divine indwelling and union in the Messiah alone; what, then, of those who extend this to every created being?

They also know that Allah has commanded obedience to Himself and His Messenger and forbidden disobedience to Himself and His Messenger; that He does not love corruption or approve of disbelief for His servants; and that created beings must worship Him by obeying His commands and seeking His help in doing so, as He said:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.”

Worshipping and obeying Him includes enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong—as far as one is able—and waging jihad in His cause against the unbelievers and hypocrites. Thus, they strive to establish His religion, seeking His help, thereby repelling and removing decreed evils and warding off those they fear may come. In the same way, a person relieves present hunger by eating and thereby wards off future hunger. Likewise, when cold weather arrives,

---

## Page 4744

he wards it off with clothing. The same applies to anything sought as a means of warding off something unwelcome. Thus, they asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about medicines we use, healing recitations we seek, and precautions we take? Do they avert any of Allah’s decree?”

He replied, “They are themselves part of Allah’s decree.”

Another hadith states:

“Supplication and affliction meet and contend with one another between heaven and earth.”

Such is the way of those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and worship Allah. All of this is worship.

Those who witness the “reality of the created order”—namely, His lordship, exalted is He, over everything—and make this a reason not to follow His religious commands laid down in revelation occupy varying degrees of misguidance. Their extremists apply this without qualification or exception, invoking divine decree to justify every violation of the Sharia.

Their position is worse than that of the Jews and Christians. It is akin to the position of the polytheists expressed in the verse:

“Those who associate others with Allah will say, ‘Had Allah willed, neither we nor our fathers would have associated others with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything.’”

They also said:

“Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them.”

These people are among the most self-contradictory on earth. Indeed, everyone who invokes divine decree as an excuse contradicts himself, for he cannot condone whatever every person does. Thus, it is inevitable, when a wrongdoer wrongs him or others, spreads corruption in the land, and begins shedding people’s blood, violating sexual sanctity, destroying crops and offspring, and committing other such forms of

---

## Page 4745

harm that make human life untenable, that he will resist this decree and punish the wrongdoer in a way that restrains the aggression of others like him.

He is therefore told: If divine decree is a valid excuse, then let everyone do whatever they wish to you and to others. If it is not an excuse, your fundamental claim that it is an excuse collapses.

Those who hold this view and invoke the “reality of the created order” do not apply their position consistently or abide by it. Rather, they follow their own opinions and desires. As one scholar said of them: “When it comes to obedience, you are a Qadarī (advocate of free will), and when it comes to sin, you are a Jabrī (advocate of compulsion). Whichever doctrine suits your desires, you adopt it.”

Among them is a “group” who claim spiritual realization and gnosis. They allege that commands and prohibitions bind only those who perceive themselves as acting and attribute deeds to themselves. As for someone who witnesses that his actions are created, or that he is compelled to perform them, and that Allah directs him just as all other moving things are moved, commands and prohibitions, promises of reward and threats of punishment no longer apply to him.

They may also say that whoever witnesses “the divine will” is no longer subject to religious obligation. One of them claims that al-Khidr was released from religious obligation because he witnessed the divine will. Thus, these people make no distinction between ordinary people and the elect who have witnessed the reality of the created order, witnessing that Allah creates His servants’ actions and governs all existing things. They may distinguish between someone who knows this intellectually and someone who perceives it through direct witnessing. They therefore do not regard religious obligation as lifted from someone who merely believes and knows this, but only from someone who

---

## Page 4746

witnesses it directly and therefore sees no action as his own whatsoever. These people do not regard compulsion and the affirmation of divine decree, as such, as precluding religious obligation. Groups claiming spiritual realization, gnosis, and affirmation of Allah’s oneness have fallen into this error.

The reason is that they could not accommodate the notion that a servant may be commanded to do something while its opposite is decreed for him, just as the Muʿtazilah and similar Qadarī groups could not accommodate it. The Muʿtazilah affirmed religious commands and prohibitions but denied divine ordainment and decree—that is, Allah’s all-encompassing will and His creation of His servants’ actions. These people, by contrast, affirmed divine ordainment and decree but denied that commands and prohibitions apply to those who witness divine decree, since they could not deny them altogether.

Their position is worse than that of the Muʿtazilah; hence none of the early generations held it. These people consider commands and prohibitions applicable to those who remain veiled and have not witnessed this reality of the created order. They therefore hold that whoever attains the witnessing of this reality is no longer bound by commands and prohibitions and has become one of the elect. They sometimes interpret the words of the Most High accordingly:

“And worship your Lord until certainty comes to you.”

They take certainty to mean knowledge of this reality. Their position is explicit disbelief, even though some groups have fallen into it without knowing that it is disbelief. For it is necessarily known in the religion of Islam that commands and prohibitions remain binding upon every servant as long as he retains his reason

---

## Page 4747

until he dies. Neither his witnessing of divine decree nor anything else releases him from commands and prohibitions. Whoever does not know this must be informed and have it explained to him. If he persists in believing that commands and prohibitions no longer apply to him, he is to be put to death.

Such doctrines have become widespread among later generations, whereas they were not known among the earlier generations of this community. These doctrines constitute defiance of Allah and His Messenger, hostility toward Him, obstruction of His path, opposition to Him, rejection of His messengers, and resistance to His judgment. Yet someone who voices these doctrines may be unaware of this and believe that the path he follows is the way of the Messenger and of Allah’s spiritually realized friends. In this respect, he is like someone who believes that prayer is not obligatory for him because the spiritual states he has attained in his heart make him independent of it; or that wine is lawful for him because he belongs to the elect, whom drinking wine does not harm; or that sexual immorality is lawful for him because he has become like the sea, which sins cannot sully; and other such beliefs.

There is no doubt that the polytheists who rejected the messengers waver between innovations contrary to Allah’s revealed law and invoking divine decree to justify disobeying Allah’s commands. Thus, these groups

---

## Page 4748

resemble the polytheists: they either introduce religious innovations, invoke divine decree to justify their actions, or combine the two.

As Allah Most High says of the polytheists:

“When they commit an indecency, they say, ‘We found our fathers doing this, and Allah has commanded us to do it.’ Say, ‘Allah does not command indecency. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?’”

And as He, Most High, says of them:

“Those who associate partners with Allah will say, ‘Had Allah willed, neither we nor our fathers would have associated partners with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything.’”

He has also described the religious practices invented by the polytheists, involving declaring the unlawful lawful and performing worship that Allah has not prescribed, in passages such as His saying, Most High:

“They say, ‘These livestock and crops are restricted; none may eat them except those we permit’—so they claim. There are livestock whose backs they forbid for riding, and livestock over which they do not mention Allah’s name, falsely attributing this to Him.”

This continues to the end of the surah.

Likewise, in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, He says:

“O children of Adam, do not let Satan tempt you as he drove your parents out of Paradise,”

up to His saying:

then to His saying:

“Say, ‘My Lord has commanded justice.’ Direct your faces toward Him at every place of worship,”

then to His saying:

“Eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not love those who are excessive.”

“Say, ‘Who has forbidden the adornment Allah has brought forth for His servants, and the good things He has provided?’”

Then to His saying:

“Say, ‘My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, whether openly or in secret; sin; unjust aggression; associating partners with Allah for which He has sent down no authority; and saying about Allah what you do not know.’”

---

## Page 4749

These people may call the religious innovations they have introduced “reality,” just as they call what they witness of divine decree “reality.” For them, the path of reality is a spiritual course whose follower is governed not by the Lawgiver’s commands and prohibitions, but by what he perceives, tastes inwardly, feels, and the like. These people do not invoke divine decree without qualification; rather, their mainstay is following their own opinions and desires. They designate what they perceive and desire as reality and command others to follow it instead of following the commands of Allah and His Messenger. This resembles the innovations of the speculative theologians—the Jahmiyyah and others—who treat the doctrines they have invented, contrary to the Quran and Sunnah, as rational truths that must be believed rather than what the revealed texts indicate.

They then either distort the Quran and Sunnah from their proper meaning or turn away from them altogether, neither reflecting upon them nor understanding them. Instead, they say, “We consign their meaning to Allah,” while believing the opposite of what they signify. When their supposed rational truths that contradict the Quran and Sunnah are subjected to scrutiny, they prove to be ignorant notions and corrupt beliefs. Likewise, when the others’ supposed realities of Allah’s friends, which contradict the Quran and Sunnah, are scrutinized, they prove to be desires followed by Allah’s enemies, not His friends.

The root of anyone’s misguidance lies in giving precedence to his own analogical reasoning over the text revealed by Allah, and in choosing desire over obedience to Allah’s commands. For inward taste, feeling, and similar experiences correspond to what a person loves: everyone who loves something has a taste and feeling proportionate to that love.

Thus, the people of faith experience inward taste and feeling of the kind explained by the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in the authentic hadith:

“Three qualities—whoever possesses them will taste the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than

---

## Page 4750

anyone else; that he loves a person only for Allah’s sake; and that he would hate to return to disbelief after Allah has saved him from it as much as he would hate to be cast into the Fire.” He, peace and blessings be upon him, also said in an authentic hadith:

“He has tasted the sweetness of faith who is content with Allah as his Lord, Islam as his religion, and Muhammad as his Prophet.”

As for the people of disbelief, religious innovation, and lust, each experiences this according to his own condition. Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah was asked, “Why are people who follow deviant inclinations so deeply attached to them?” He replied, “Have you forgotten His words, Most High: ‘Because of their disbelief, their hearts were steeped in love of the calf’?”—or words to that effect.

Idol worshippers love their gods, as Allah Most High says:

“Among people are those who take others besides Allah as equals, loving them as they love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah.”

He also says:

“If they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desires without guidance from Allah?”

And He says:

“They follow nothing but conjecture and what their souls desire, although guidance has come to them from their Lord.”

This is why these people are drawn to listening to poetry and vocal performances that stir love in general—a love not exclusive to the people of faith, but shared by those who love the Most Merciful, idols, crosses, homelands, companions, beardless youths, or women. These are the people who follow their inward tastes and feelings without assessing them against the Quran, the Sunnah, and the way of the early generations of the Muslim community.

Anyone who departs from what Allah sent His Messenger with—worshipping and obeying Him and obeying His Messenger—is not following a religion prescribed by Allah. As He, Most High, says:

“Then We set you upon a clear way in matters of religion, so follow it

---

## Page 4751

and do not follow the desires of those who do not know.”

“They will be of no avail to you against Allah,” up to His words: “And Allah is the Protector of the righteous.”

Rather, such a person follows his own desires without guidance from Allah. Allah Most High says:

“Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them a religion that Allah has not authorized?”

In this, they sometimes follow an innovation that they call a spiritual reality, giving it precedence over what Allah has prescribed. At other times, they invoke Allah’s decree governing creation to oppose His revealed law, as Allah has related concerning the polytheists, as mentioned earlier.

Among these people is a group who rank highest among them. They adhere to the religion by performing its well-known obligations and avoiding its well-known prohibitions. Yet they err by abandoning the means they have been commanded to pursue that are themselves acts of worship. They suppose that once a person of spiritual knowledge witnesses “the divine decree,” he turns away from such things. For example, some of them regard reliance upon Allah, supplication, and similar practices as spiritual stations for ordinary people, not the elect. This rests on the notion that whoever witnesses the divine decree knows that whatever has been decreed will come to pass, so there is no need for such practices. This is a grave error.

Allah has decreed things together with the means that bring them about, just as He has decreed felicity and wretchedness together with their means. As the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Allah created people for Paradise. He created it for them while they were still in their fathers’ loins, and they perform the deeds of the people of Paradise.”

Likewise, when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, informed them that Allah had written down all that was decreed, they asked:

“O Messenger of Allah, should we not then abandon deeds and rely on what has been written?”

He replied:

“No. Act, for everyone will be enabled to do that for which he was created. Whoever is among the people of felicity will be enabled to perform the deeds of the people of felicity, and whoever is among the people of wretchedness will be enabled to perform the deeds of the people of wretchedness.”

## Page 4752

Thus, the means that Allah has commanded His servants to pursue are themselves acts of worship. Reliance upon Allah is coupled with worship, as in His words:

“So worship Him and put your trust in Him.”

And His words:

“Say, ‘He is my Lord; there is no god but Him. In Him I have put my trust, and to Him I turn in repentance.’”

And the words of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him:

“In Him I have put my trust, and to Him I turn.”

Among them are some who may abandon recommended deeds, though not obligatory ones, and thus fall short to that extent. Others are deluded by extraordinary occurrences they experience, such as spiritual unveilings, prayers answered in ways that depart from the ordinary course of events, and similar things. These distract them from the worship, gratitude, and other duties they have been commanded to observe. Such things frequently befall those pursuing the spiritual path and turning towards Allah. A servant escapes them only by adhering at all times to Allah’s command, with which He sent His Messenger.

As al-Zuhrī said:

“Those of our predecessors who came before us used to say, ‘Holding fast to the Sunnah is salvation.’”

For the Sunnah—as Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, said—is like Noah’s ark: whoever boards it is saved, and whoever stays behind drowns.

Worship, obedience, uprightness, adherence to the straight path, and similar expressions all convey the same meaning, and they have two foundations:

## Page 4753

the first is that none but Allah should be worshipped; the second is that He should be worshipped through what He has commanded and prescribed, not through innovations.

Allah Most High says:

“So whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and associate no one in the worship of his Lord.”

And He says:

“Yes, whoever submits himself to Allah while doing good will have his reward with his Lord. No fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve.”

And He says:

“And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while doing good and follows the religion of Abraham, upright in faith? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.”

Righteous action means doing good—that is, performing good deeds. “Good deeds” are those that Allah and His Messenger love: whatever He has commanded as obligatory or recommended. Religious innovations that have not been prescribed are loved neither by Allah nor by His Messenger, so they are neither good deeds nor righteous actions. Likewise, committing forbidden acts, such as indecencies and injustice, is neither a good deed nor a righteous action.

As for His words:

“And associate no one in the worship of his Lord,”

and His words:

“Submits himself to Allah,”

these mean devoting one’s religion sincerely to Allah alone. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb used to say: “O Allah, make all my deeds righteous, make them sincerely for Your sake, and give no one else any share in them.”

Regarding His words:

“To test you as to which of you is best in deeds,”

al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyād said: “The most sincere and the most correct.” They asked: “Abū ‘Alī, what does ‘the most sincere and the most correct’ mean?” He replied:

---

## Page 4754

“If a deed is sincere but not correct, it will not be accepted. If it is correct but not sincere, it will not be accepted, until it is both sincere and correct. Sincerity means that it is done for Allah, and correctness means that it accords with the Sunnah.”

If it is asked: Since everything Allah loves falls within the meaning of worship, why are other things mentioned alongside it, as in His words:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help,”

and His words:

“So worship Him and put your trust in Him,”

and the words of Noah:

“Worship Allah, fear Him, and obey me,”

and similar statements by other messengers?

The answer is that there are parallels to this, as in His words:

“Indeed, prayer restrains from indecency and wrongdoing.”

Indecency is itself a form of wrongdoing. Likewise, He says:

“Indeed, Allah commands justice, doing good, and giving to relatives, and forbids indecency, wrongdoing, and oppression.”

Giving to relatives is part of justice and doing good, just as indecency and oppression are forms of wrongdoing.

Likewise, He says:

“And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer.”

Establishing prayer is among the greatest ways of holding fast to the Book.

Likewise, He says:

“Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and call upon Us in hope and fear.”

Their calling upon Him in hope and fear is itself among those good deeds. There are many such examples in the Quran.

Sometimes, in this type of expression, one thing is included within the other but is mentioned alongside it to single it out for special mention, since it is required both under the general meaning and in its own specific capacity. At other times, a term’s scope varies depending on whether it occurs alone or alongside another term: when used alone, its meaning is general; when paired with another, its meaning is specific. Examples are the terms “poor” and “needy”: when

---

## Page 4755

either is used alone, as in His words:

“For the poor who are restricted in the cause of Allah,”

and His words:

“Its expiation is to feed ten needy people,”

the other is included within its meaning. But when they are mentioned together in His words:

“Alms are only for the poor and the needy,”

they denote two distinct categories.

It has been said that when a specific term is mentioned alongside a general term, it is not included within the general term in that context; rather, this falls into the category just described. The correct view, however, is that this is not necessarily so. Allah Most High says:

“Whoever is an enemy to Allah, His angels, His messengers, Gabriel and Michael,”

and He says:

“And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary.”

A specific term may be mentioned alongside a general term for various reasons. Sometimes it possesses a distinctive quality not shared by the other members of the general category, as with Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. At other times, the general term is expressed without qualification, so its comprehensive scope may not be understood, as in His words:

“A guidance for the Allah-fearing,”

“Who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided them,”

“And who believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you.”

His words, “believe in the unseen,” encompass the unseen matters in which belief is obligatory. Yet the expression is general and does not itself indicate that what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you are included among those unseen matters. The intended meaning may also be that they believe both in what is conveyed—the unseen—and in the revelation conveying news of the unseen, namely, what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you.

Likewise, He said to Moses:

Reliance upon Allah and seeking His help are themselves part of worshipping Him. Yet they are singled out for mention so that the worshipper makes a deliberate point of practising them, for they provide help in all other forms of worship: He, glorified is He, can only be worshipped with His help.

Once this is clear, a created being’s perfection lies in fully realizing its servitude to Allah. The more fully a servant realizes this servitude, the greater his perfection and the higher his rank. Anyone who imagines that a created being can escape servitude in any respect, or that leaving it behind is a more perfect state, is among the most ignorant and misguided of all creatures.
