## Page 4760

Section

Now that this is clear, it is evident that people differ greatly in this regard, reflecting their differing degrees in the reality of faith. In this respect, they fall into general and special categories. Accordingly, the Lord’s lordship over them has both a general and a special aspect. This is why associating partners with Allah within this community is subtler than the creeping of ants.

It is related in the Sahīh that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“May the slave of the dirham come to ruin! May the slave of the dinar come to ruin! May the slave of plush fabric come to ruin! May the slave of the patterned cloak come to ruin! May he come to ruin and be cast down! If a thorn pricks him, may it not be removed! If he is given something, he is pleased; if he is denied it, he is displeased.”

Thus, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, called him the slave of the dirham, the slave of the dinar, the slave of plush fabric, and the slave of the patterned cloak. He also spoke words containing both an imprecation and a statement:

“May he come to ruin and be cast down! If a thorn pricks him, may it not be removed!”

Naqsh means removing a thorn from the foot, and a minqāsh is the instrument used to remove it. Such is the condition of someone who, when afflicted by harm, neither escapes it nor prospers, having come to ruin and been cast down. He neither attains what he seeks nor escapes what he dislikes. This is the condition of one who worships wealth. He is described as follows:

“When he is given something, he is pleased; when he is denied it, he is displeased.”

As Allah Most High says:

“Among them are those who criticize you concerning the distribution of alms. If

---

## Page 4761

they are given some of it, they are pleased; but if they are given none, they become displeased.” Their pleasure and displeasure are thus for something other than Allah. Such is also the condition of someone attached to a position of authority, an outward form, or any similar object of his own desire: if he obtains it, he is pleased; if he does not, he is displeased. He is therefore the slave of whatever he desires, held in bondage to it. For slavery and servitude are, in reality, the slavery and servitude of the heart. Whatever enslaves and subjugates his heart makes him its slave.

Hence the saying:

“The slave is free so long as he is content, and the free man is a slave so long as he covets.”

A poet said:

“I obeyed my cravings, and they enslaved me;
Had I been content, I would have been free.”

It is also said: “Covetousness is a shackle around the neck and a fetter on the foot. When the shackle leaves the neck, the fetter leaves the foot.”

It is related that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“Covetousness is poverty, and giving up hope is freedom from need. When any of you gives up hope of something, he no longer needs it.”

A person can recognize this within himself. When he gives up hope of something, he neither seeks nor covets it, nor does he keep his heart dependent upon it or upon whoever might bring it about. But when he covets something and hopes for it, his heart becomes attached to it. He then becomes dependent on obtaining it and on anyone he believes instrumental in securing it. This applies to wealth, prestige, outward forms, and other things. Allah’s close friend, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“So seek provision from Allah, worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.”

---

## Page 4762

A servant must have provision and is in need of it. If he seeks his provision from Allah, he becomes Allah’s servant, dependent upon Him; but if he seeks it from a created being, he becomes that being’s servant, dependent upon him. This is why “asking of created beings” is prohibited in principle and is permitted only out of necessity. Many hadiths prohibit it in the Sahīh, Sunan, and Musnad collections, such as the Prophet’s saying, peace and blessings be upon him:

“One of you will persist in begging until he comes on the Day of Resurrection without a shred of flesh on his face.”

And his saying:

“Whoever asks people when he has enough to meet his needs will find his asking turned into scratches, claw marks, or gashes on his face on the Day of Resurrection.”

And his saying:

“Begging is not lawful except for someone burdened with an overwhelming debt, anguished weeping, or grinding poverty.”

This meaning is reported in the Sahīh collection. It also contains:

“For one of you to take his rope and go out to gather firewood is better for him than asking people, whether they give to him or refuse him.”

He also said:

“Whatever comes to you of this wealth without your asking for it or eagerly looking for it, take it. Whatever does not come to you, do not let your soul pursue it.”

He thus disapproved of taking it through verbal requests or inward longing. He said in an authentic hadith:

“Whoever seeks to be free of need, Allah will make him free of need; whoever seeks to refrain from asking, Allah will enable him to refrain; whoever strives to be patient, Allah will grant him patience. No one has been given a gift better or more ample than patience.”

He instructed his closest Companions not to ask people for anything. It is reported in the Musnad:

“When Abū Bakr’s whip fell from his hand, he would not say to anyone, ‘Hand it to me.’ He would say, ‘My close friend instructed me not to ask people for anything.’”

In Sahīh Muslim and elsewhere, it is narrated from ‘Awf ibn Mālik “that

---

## Page 4763

the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, accepted his pledge of allegiance along with a group of others and quietly confided to them: ‘Do not ask people for anything.’ There were men among that group who, if their whip fell from their hand, would not say to anyone, ‘Hand it to me.’”

In numerous places, the scriptural texts command asking the Creator and prohibit asking created beings. For example, Allah Most High says:

“So when you are free, strive hard, and direct your longing to your Lord.”

And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Ibn ‘Abbās:

“When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah.”

Another example is the statement of Abraham, Allah’s close friend:

“So seek from Allah your provision.”

He did not say, “So seek your provision from Allah,” because placing the adverbial phrase first suggests exclusivity and restriction. It is as though he said, “Seek provision from none but Allah.”

Allah Most High also says:

“And ask Allah of His bounty.”

A person must obtain the provision and other things he needs and ward off whatever harms him. In both matters, he is instructed to direct his supplication to Allah. He may ask Allah and bring his complaints to Him, as Jacob, peace be upon him, said:

“I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah.”

Allah Most High mentions in the Quran “gracious withdrawal,” “gracious forgiveness,” and “gracious patience.”

It has been said that gracious withdrawal is withdrawal without causing harm; gracious forgiveness is forgiveness without reproach; and gracious patience is patience without complaining to created beings. Thus, during Ahmad ibn Hanbal’s illness, it was read to him that Tāwūs disapproved of the groaning

---

## Page 4764

of the sick, saying, “It is a form of complaint.” Thereafter, Ahmad did not groan until his death. Complaining to the Creator, however, does not conflict with gracious patience, for Jacob said:

“So gracious patience is best.”

He also said:

“I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah.”

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, used to recite the surahs Jonah, Joseph, and The Bee in the dawn prayer. When he came to this verse in his recitation, he wept until his sobbing could be heard from the back rows.

Among the supplications of Moses was:

“O Allah, to You belongs all praise; to You complaints are brought; You are the One whose help is sought; from You relief is sought; and upon You we rely. There is neither might nor power except through You.”

In the supplication the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, made after the people of Tāʾif treated him as they did, he said:

“O Allah, to You I complain of my weakness, my lack of resources, and my low standing among people. You are the Lord of the oppressed, and You are my Lord. O Allah, to whom will You entrust me? To a stranger who receives me harshly, or to an enemy whom You have given power over me? If You are not angry with me, I do not mind, though Your protection from affliction would bring me greater ease. I seek refuge in the light of Your Face, through which darkness is dispelled and the affairs of this world and the Hereafter are set right, lest Your displeasure descend upon me or Your anger fall upon me. It is for me to seek Your pleasure until You are pleased. For there is neither might nor power except through You.”

In some narrations: “And there is neither might nor power except through You.”

The stronger a servant’s longing for Allah’s bounty and mercy, and his hope that Allah will fulfil his needs and relieve his distress, the stronger his servitude to Him and his freedom from everything besides Him. Just as placing his hopes in a created being brings him into servitude to that being, giving up hope in him makes his heart independent of him.

As it has been said:

“Be independent

---

## Page 4765

of whomever you wish, and you will be his equal; give generously to whomever you wish, and you will be his master; be in need of whomever you wish, and you will be his captive.”

Likewise, a servant’s longing for his Lord’s bounty and his hope in Him bring him into servitude to Him. His heart’s turning away from asking anyone other than Allah, and from placing hope in Him, causes his heart to turn away from servitude to Allah. This is especially so of someone who places his hopes in created beings rather than the Creator: his heart relies either on his authority, troops, followers, and slaves; on his family and friends; on his wealth and reserves; or on his masters and dignitaries—such as his owner, king, shaykh, patron, and others who have already died or will die.

Allah Most High says:

“And put your trust in the Ever-Living, who does not die, and glorify Him with praise. Sufficient is He as One fully aware of His servants’ sins.”

Whoever attaches his heart to created beings, expecting them to help him, provide for him, or guide him, becomes inwardly submissive to them. His heart becomes enslaved to them in proportion to that attachment, even if outwardly he is their ruler, directing their affairs and exercising authority over them. A sensible person looks at realities, not appearances.

When a man’s heart becomes attached to a woman, even one lawful for him, his heart remains her captive: she rules it and controls it as she wishes. Outwardly, he is her master because he is her husband, but in reality he is her captive and slave. This is especially so if she knows how much he needs her, how passionately he loves her, and that he would accept no other woman in her place. She then rules him as an overpowering, unjust master rules his subjugated slave, who cannot escape

---

## Page 4766

from him. Indeed, her domination is greater still, for captivity of the heart is more severe than captivity of the body, and enslavement of the heart is more severe than enslavement of the body. Someone whose body has been enslaved and reduced to bondage may be untroubled so long as his heart remains free of it and at peace. He may even devise a means of escape. But when the heart—which is the ruler—is itself in bondage, enslaved and enthralled by something other than Allah, this is utter humiliation and captivity, and servitude to whatever has enslaved the heart.

It is the heart’s servitude and captivity that entail reward and punishment. If a Muslim is captured by an unbeliever or wrongfully enslaved by an evildoer, that does not harm him so long as he fulfils whatever obligations he can. Someone lawfully enslaved receives two rewards if he fulfils his duties towards Allah and towards his masters. Even if he is compelled to utter words of unbelief and does so while his heart remains secure in faith, that does not harm him. But someone whose heart has become enslaved, making him a slave to something other than Allah, is harmed by this even if outwardly he is the king of all people.

True freedom is freedom of the heart, and true servitude is servitude of the heart, just as true wealth is wealth of the soul. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Wealth does not consist in having many possessions; rather, true wealth is richness of the soul.”

All this, indeed, concerns someone whose heart has been enslaved by the beauty of a person lawful for him. But someone whose heart has been enslaved by the beauty of a person forbidden to him—a woman or a boy—experiences torment for which there is no recompense. Such people are among those who suffer the greatest torment and receive the least reward. For when someone enamoured of another’s beauty remains attached to that person in his heart and enslaved to them, there accumulate for him

---

## Page 4767

such kinds of evil and corruption as none but the Lord of all servants can enumerate, even if he avoids committing the grave act of sexual immorality. For the heart’s persistent attachment to that person, even without committing sexual immorality, is more harmful to him than committing a sin and then repenting of it until its traces disappear from his heart. Such people are likened to the intoxicated and the insane.

As it has been said:

“Two intoxications: the intoxication of passion and that of wine—
When will someone gripped by both regain his senses?”

And it has been said:

“They said, ‘You have gone mad over the one you love.’ I replied,
‘Passion is worse than the madness of the insane.
One stricken by passion never regains his senses throughout his life,
Whereas the madman is seized only from time to time.’”

One of the greatest causes of this affliction is the heart’s turning away from Allah. Once the heart tastes the sweetness of worshipping Allah and being sincerely devoted to Him, nothing is ever sweeter, more delightful, or more pleasant to it. A person gives up something he loves only for something else he loves more, or out of fear of something unwelcome. Thus, the heart turns away from corrupt love only through wholesome love or fear of harm.

---

## Page 4768

Allah Most High said concerning Joseph:

“Thus it was, that We might turn evil and immorality away from him. Indeed, he was one of Our chosen servants.”

Through His servant’s sincere devotion to Him, Allah turns away from him the harmful attraction and attachment to outward forms, and keeps him from sexual immorality. Thus, before a person tastes the sweetness of servitude to Allah and sincere devotion to Him, his soul overpowers him, making him follow its desires. But once he tastes sincere devotion and it grows strong in his heart, his desires yield to it without any need for remedial measures.

Allah Most High said:

“Indeed, prayer restrains one from immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater.”

Prayer both wards off what is unwelcome—immorality and wrongdoing—and brings about what is beloved: the remembrance of Allah. Attaining what is beloved is greater than warding off what is unwelcome, for remembering Allah is worshipping Him, and the heart’s worship of Allah is sought for its own sake. By contrast, warding evil off from the heart is sought for a further purpose, as a subsidiary aim. The heart was created to love, desire, and seek the truth.

When the desire for evil arises within it, it seeks to repel that desire, for it corrupts the heart just as weeds growing among crops ruin them. Hence Allah Most High said:

“Successful indeed is the one who purifies it, and failed indeed is the one who corrupts it.”

And Allah Most High said:

“Successful indeed is the one who purifies himself, remembers the name of his Lord, and prays.”

And He said:

“Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their chastity. That is purer for them.”

And Allah Most High said:

“Were it not for Allah’s bounty and mercy upon you, not one of you would ever have become pure.”

Thus He, glorified be He, has declared lowering the gaze and guarding chastity to be more purifying

---

## Page 4769

for the soul, and has made it clear that abandoning immoral acts is part of purifying the soul. Purifying the soul entails removing all evils, including immorality, injustice, associating partners with Allah, lying, and other such things.

Likewise, one who seeks leadership and supremacy on earth is, at heart, enslaved to those who help him attain them. Although outwardly he may be their leader whom they obey, in reality he places his hopes in them and fears them. He lavishes wealth and positions of authority upon them and pardons them so that they will obey and support him. Outwardly, he is a leader who is obeyed; in reality, he is their obedient slave. The truth is that each party is, in some measure, enslaved to the other, and both have abandoned true worship of Allah. If they cooperate in seeking unjust supremacy on earth, they are like two people cooperating in sexual immorality or highway robbery. Each is enslaved by the other because of the desire that has enslaved and enthralled him.

The same applies to one who seeks wealth: it enslaves and enthralls him. These things are of two kinds:

(One kind)
comprises things a person needs, such as food, drink, housing, marriage, and the like. He seeks these from Allah and turns to Him in desire for them. Wealth is then something he uses to meet his needs, like the donkey he rides or the mat he sits upon—indeed, like the privy in which he relieves himself—without becoming enslaved to it and thus becoming fretful

---

## Page 4770

—distressed when adversity befalls him, and withholding when good comes his way.

The other kind comprises things a person does not need. He should not attach his heart to these, for if he does, he becomes enslaved to them. He may even come to rely on other than Allah, so that he no longer truly worships Allah or truly relies upon Him. Rather, he has within him an element of worshipping other than Allah and an element of relying upon other than Allah. He is among those to whom the words of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, most aptly apply:

“May the slave of the dirham come to ruin! May the slave of the dinar come to ruin! May the slave of the plush cloak come to ruin! May the slave of the patterned cloak come to ruin!”

Such a person is enslaved to these things, even if he asks Allah for them: if Allah grants them to him, he is pleased; if He withholds them, he is displeased. The true servant of Allah, however, is one who is pleased by what pleases Allah and displeased by what displeases Allah; who loves what Allah and His Messenger love and hates what Allah and His Messenger hate; and who allies himself with Allah’s allies and opposes Allah’s enemies. Such a person has perfected his faith, as stated in the hadith:

“Whoever loves for Allah’s sake, hates for Allah’s sake, gives for Allah’s sake, and withholds for Allah’s sake has perfected his faith.”

He also said:

“The firmest bonds of faith are love for Allah’s sake and hatred for Allah’s sake.”

An authentic report from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, states:

“Whoever possesses three qualities will taste the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than all else; that he loves a person solely for Allah’s sake; and that he abhors returning to disbelief after Allah has saved him from it just as he abhors being cast into the Fire.”

Thus, this person is in accord with his Lord in what He loves and what

---

## Page 4771

He hates. Thus Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than all else, and he loves a created being for Allah’s sake, not for any other purpose. This is part of the perfection of his love for Allah, for loving those whom one’s beloved loves is part of loving the beloved fully. Thus, if he loves Allah’s prophets and allies because they uphold what the True One loves, and for no other reason, then he loves them for Allah’s sake alone.

Allah Most High says:

“Allah will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble towards the believers, mighty against the disbelievers.”

For this reason, Allah Most High says:

“Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you.”

The Messenger commands what Allah loves, forbids what Allah hates, does what Allah loves, and conveys what Allah loves to be believed. Whoever loves Allah must therefore follow the Messenger: believing what he reports, obeying what he commands, and following his example in what he does. Whoever does this has done what Allah loves, and Allah will therefore love him.

Allah has thus given two signs by which those who love Him are known: following the Messenger and jihad in His cause. For jihad, in essence, consists in striving to bring about what Allah loves of faith and righteous deeds, and to repel what Allah hates of disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience.

Allah Most High says:

“Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, and your clan”

—up to His words:

“until Allah brings about His command.”

With this warning, He threatens those whose families and wealth are dearer to them than Allah, His Messenger, and jihad in His cause.

Indeed, it is authentically reported from the Prophet that he said:

“By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one truly believes

---

## Page 4772

until I am dearer to him than his children, his father, and all other people.”

It is also authentically reported that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb said to him, “O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, you are dearer to me than everything except myself.” He replied, “No, ʿUmar—not until I am dearer to you than your own self.” ʿUmar said, “Then, by Allah, you are dearer to me than my own self.” He replied, “Now, ʿUmar.”

True love is only complete through loyalty to the beloved: sharing his love for what he loves and his hatred for what he hates. Allah loves faith and piety, and hates disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience.

It is well known that love moves the heart’s will. The stronger love becomes in the heart, the more the heart seeks to do what is loved. When love is complete, it necessarily produces a firm resolve to bring about what is loved. If the servant is able to do so, he accomplishes it. If he is unable but does whatever lies within his capacity, he receives a reward like that of the one who actually accomplishes it. As the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without that diminishing their rewards in the least. Whoever calls to misguidance will bear a burden of sin like the burdens of those who follow him, without that diminishing their burdens in the least.”

He also said:

“There are men in Medina who have been with you on every journey you have made and in every valley you have crossed.”

They asked, “Even though they are in Medina?”

He replied, “Even though they are in Medina. They were held back by a valid excuse.”

Jihad means exerting one’s utmost effort—that is, all that lies within one’s capacity—to bring about what the True One loves

---

## Page 4773

and warding off what the True One hates. If the servant neglects whatever jihad lies within his capacity, this indicates the weakness of his love for Allah and His Messenger in his heart.

It is well known that what one loves generally cannot be attained without enduring what one dislikes, whether that love is sound or corrupt. Those who love wealth, authority, and physical beauty attain their goals only by suffering harm in this world, besides the harm that befalls them in this world and the Hereafter. Thus, if someone who loves Allah and His Messenger does not endure the hardships that discerning lovers of things other than Allah consider necessary and themselves endure to attain what they love, this indicates weakness in their love for Allah—provided that the course those others follow is one that reason recommends. It is well known that the believer is stronger in his love for Allah. As the Most High says:

“Among people are those who take others besides Allah as equals, loving them as they love Allah.”

Admittedly, a lover may, through poor judgment and a flawed understanding, follow a path that does not lead to the desired goal. Such a path is not commendable when the love itself is sound and praiseworthy; how much less so when the love is corrupt and the path does not lead to the goal! This is what reckless seekers of wealth, authority, and physical beauty do in loving things that bring them harm without securing what they seek. What is meant here is only the paths that reason follows to attain its goal.

Once this is clear, the more the heart grows in love for Allah, the more it grows in servitude to Him; and the more it grows in servitude to Him, the more it grows in love for Him and in freedom from everything besides Him. The heart is inherently in need

---

## Page 4774

of Allah in “two respects”: in worship, which is the final cause, and in seeking help and placing trust in Him, which is the efficient cause. The heart cannot be sound or prosper, nor find pleasure, joy, well-being, rest, or reassurance, except by worshipping its Lord, loving Him, and turning to Him. Even if it obtained every created thing that gives it pleasure, it would find neither reassurance nor rest, for it has an inherent need for its Lord as the One it worships, loves, and seeks. Through this it attains joy, happiness, pleasure, bliss, rest, and reassurance.

Yet it can attain this only through Allah’s help; none but Allah can bring it about for the heart. Thus, it constantly needs the reality expressed in:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.”

For even if a person were helped to obtain what he loves, seeks, craves, and desires, yet did not attain the worship of Allah—making Him the ultimate object of his desire, his highest aim, and the primary object of his love, loving everything else only for His sake and loving nothing for its own sake except Allah—then, without this, he would not have realized the true meaning of “There is no god worthy of worship but Allah,” nor truly attained monotheism, servitude, and love. His deficiency and imperfection—indeed, his pain, regret, and torment—would be proportionate to that failure.

Even if he strove to attain this goal, he would not attain it unless he sought Allah’s help, placed his trust in Him, and acknowledged his need for Him in attaining it. For whatever Allah wills comes to pass, and whatever He does not will does not come to pass. Thus, he needs Allah in that He is the One sought, loved, desired, and worshipped, and in

---

## Page 4775

that He is the One petitioned, whose help is sought, and in whom trust is placed. He is his God, and he has no god besides Him; He is his Lord, and he has no lord besides Him. His servitude to Allah is complete only through these two aspects. Whenever he loves something other than Allah for its own sake, or looks to something other than Allah to help him, he becomes a servant of what he loves and of what he places his hope in, in proportion to his love and hope.

But if he loves none but Allah for His own sake, loves everything else only for His sake, and never places his hope in anything but Allah; and if, whatever means he employs or acquires, he remains conscious that Allah created and ordained them, and that Allah is the Lord, Sovereign, and Creator of everything in the heavens and the earth, all of which stands in need of Him—then he has attained completeness in his servitude to Allah in proportion to the share of this he has been granted.

People differ greatly in their degrees of attainment in this regard, across a range that only Allah can fully encompass. Those who are most perfect, best, highest in rank, closest to Allah, strongest, and best guided are those whose servitude to Allah is most complete in this respect.

This is the true essence of the religion of Islam with which He sent His messengers and revealed His Books: that the servant submit to Allah and to no other. Whoever submits to Him and to another associates partners with Him, while whoever refuses to submit to Him is arrogant. It is authentically reported from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“No one with an atom’s weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise, just as

---

## Page 4776

no one with an atom’s weight of faith in his heart will enter the Fire.” He thus set arrogance in opposition to faith, for arrogance is incompatible with the true essence of servitude, as is established in an authentic report from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Allah says: ‘Greatness is My lower garment and grandeur My upper garment. Whoever contests either of them with Me, I will punish him.’”

Greatness and grandeur belong exclusively to lordship, and grandeur is higher than greatness. Hence He likened grandeur to the upper garment and greatness to the lower garment. This is why the proclamation “Allah is the Greatest” is the hallmark of the prayers, the call to prayer, and the festivals. It is also recommended in elevated places such as al-Safā and al-Marwah, when one ascends a height or mounts a riding animal, and in similar circumstances. By it, a fire is extinguished, however great, and at the call to prayer Satan flees.

Allah Most High says:

“And your Lord says, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation.’”

Everyone who is too arrogant to worship Allah must inevitably worship something else, for a human being is a sentient being who acts by will. It is authentically reported from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said:

“The most truthful names are Hārith and Hammām.”

Hārith means one who earns and acts, while Hammām is an intensive form derived from hamm (intention), and intention is the first stage of willing. A human being is always willing something, and every act of will must have an ultimate object. Every servant must therefore have a beloved object of desire that is the ultimate goal of his love and will. Whoever does not take Allah as the One he worships and the ultimate goal of his love and will, but is instead too arrogant to do so, must inevitably have a beloved object of desire

---

## Page 4777

other than Allah that enslaves him. He thus becomes a slave to that beloved object of desire—whether wealth, prestige, physical beauty, or something he takes as a deity besides Allah, such as the sun, the moon, the stars, idols, or the graves of prophets and righteous people; or angels and prophets whom he takes as lords; or anything else worshipped besides Allah. If he is a slave to something other than Allah, he associates partners with Allah. Every arrogant person associates partners with Allah. Thus Pharaoh was among the most arrogant of all creatures in refusing to worship Allah, and he associated partners with Him.

Allah Most High says:

“And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority to Pharaoh, Haman and Qārūn, but they said, ‘A magician and a liar.’”

Further on, He says:

“And Moses said, ‘Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant person who does not believe in the Day of Account.’”

And further on:

“Thus does Allah seal the heart of every arrogant tyrant.”

Allah Most High also says:

“And Qārūn, Pharaoh and Haman—Moses had certainly come to them with clear proofs, but they were arrogant in the land, and they could not escape Us.”

Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and divided its people into factions, oppressing a group among them, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive. Indeed, he was one of the corrupters.”

There are many similar passages in the Quran.

Pharaoh is also described as associating partners with Allah in His words:

“And the chiefs among Pharaoh’s people said, ‘Will you leave Moses and his people to spread corruption in the land and abandon you and your gods?’”

---

## Page 4778

Rather, examining the evidence shows that the more arrogantly a person refuses to worship Allah, the more he associates partners with Him. For the more arrogantly he refuses to worship Allah, the greater his dependence upon and need for the beloved object of his desire—the heart’s primary object of pursuit. He thus participates in such association through whatever of these things has enslaved him.

The heart can never become independent of all created beings unless Allah is its Master: it worships none but Him, seeks help from none but Him, relies upon none but Him, rejoices only in what He loves and approves, and dislikes only what the Lord hates and dislikes. It allies itself only with those whom Allah befriends and opposes only those whom Allah opposes. It loves only for Allah’s sake, hates anything only for Allah’s sake, gives only for Allah’s sake, and withholds only for Allah’s sake. The more sincerely a person devotes his religion to Allah alone, the more complete his servitude and independence of created beings become. Through complete servitude to Allah, he is freed from arrogance and associating partners with Him.

Associating partners with Allah predominates among Christians, while arrogance predominates among Jews. Allah Most High says concerning Christians:

“They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah, and also the Messiah, the son of Mary, although they were commanded only to worship one God. There is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.”

He says concerning Jews:

“Is it that whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, you became arrogant? Some you denied, and others you killed.”

Allah Most High also says:

“I will turn away from My signs those who behave arrogantly on earth without right. And even if they see

---

## Page 4779

every sign, they will not believe in it. And if they see the path of right guidance, they will not take it as their way; but if they see the path of error, they will take it as their way.”

Arrogance necessarily entails associating partners with Allah, which is the opposite of Islam and the sin that Allah does not forgive. Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives whatever is less than that for whomever He wills. Whoever associates partners with Allah has indeed committed a tremendous sin.”

He also says:

“Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives whatever is less than that for whomever He wills. Whoever associates partners with Allah has indeed strayed far astray.”

Thus, all the prophets were sent with the religion of Islam. It is the religion besides which Allah accepts no other, whether from earlier or later generations.

Noah said:

“But if you turn away, I have asked you for no payment. My reward is only with Allah, and I have been commanded to be among the Muslims.”

Allah says concerning Abraham:

“And who would turn away from the faith of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself? We certainly chose him in this world, and in the Hereafter he will surely be among the righteous.”

“When his Lord said to him, ‘Submit,’ he said, ‘I have submitted to the Lord of all worlds.’”

Then, further on, He says:

“So do not die except as Muslims.”

Joseph said:

“Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous.”

Moses said:

“O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then put your trust in Him, if you are Muslims.”

“They said, ‘In Allah we have put our trust.’”

Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, We sent down the Torah, containing guidance and light. By it, the prophets who submitted to Allah judged for the Jews.”

Bilqīs said:

“My Lord, I have indeed wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to Allah, the Lord of all worlds.”

And He says:

---

## Page 4780

“And when I inspired the disciples, ‘Believe in Me and in My messenger,’ they said, ‘We believe, so bear witness that we are Muslims.’”

And He says:

“Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam.”

And He says:

“Whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Do they seek a religion other than Allah’s, when all those in the heavens and the earth have submitted to Him, willingly or unwillingly?”

He thus mentions the submission of all beings, willingly or unwillingly, because all creatures are His servants in the universal sense, whether they acknowledge this or deny it. They are subject to His authority and governance, submitting to Him willingly or unwillingly. No creature can escape what He has willed, ordained, and decreed, and there is no might or power except through Him. He is the Lord and Sovereign of all worlds, directing them however He wills. He is the Creator, Originator, and Fashioner of them all. Everything besides Him is subject to His lordship: made, brought into being, dependent, needy, enslaved, and subdued. He is the One, the Subduer, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner.

Although He has created what He has created through causes, He is the Creator of each cause and the One who ordains it; the cause is dependent upon Him just as its effect is. No created cause can independently bring anything about or ward off harm. Rather, every cause needs another cause to assist it, as well as something to repel whatever opposes and obstructs it. He alone—glory be to Him—is entirely free of need of everything besides Him. He has no partner to assist Him and no adversary to resist or oppose Him.

Allah Most High says:

“Say, ‘Have you considered those you invoke besides

---

## Page 4781

Allah—if Allah intended harm for me, could they remove His harm? Or if He intended mercy for me, could they withhold His mercy?’ Say, ‘Allah is sufficient for me; in Him let those who trust place their trust.’”

The Most High also says:

“If Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it except Him; and if He touches you with good, He has power over all things.”

The Most High also relates the words of His intimate friend, Abraham:

“O my people, I am free of whatever you associate with Allah.”

“Indeed, I have turned my face toward Him who created the heavens and the earth, inclining to Him alone, and I am not one of the polytheists.”

“His people argued with him. He said, ‘Do you argue with me about Allah when He has guided me? I do not fear what you associate with Him, unless my Lord should will something.’”

And so on, up to His words:

“Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrongdoing—it is they who will have security, and it is they who are rightly guided.”

It is reported in the two Sahīh collections from Ibn Mas‘ūd, may Allah be pleased with him, that when this verse was revealed, it troubled the Prophet’s Companions, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. They said, “O Messenger of Allah, which of us has not mixed his faith with wrongdoing?” He replied, “It refers only to associating partners with Allah. Have you not heard the words of the righteous servant: ‘Indeed, associating partners with Allah is a tremendous wrong’?”

Abraham, Allah’s intimate friend, is the leader of the sincere monotheists. He was sent when the religion of the polytheists had spread throughout the earth. Allah Most High says:

“And when Abraham’s Lord tested him with commands, which he fulfilled, He said, ‘I will make you a leader for the people.’ Abraham said, ‘And from among my descendants?’ He said, ‘My covenant does not extend to the wrongdoers.’”

He thus made clear that His covenant concerning leadership does not extend to a wrongdoer. Allah, glory be to Him, therefore did not command that a wrongdoer be a leader. And the greatest wrongdoing is associating partners with Allah.

---

## Page 4782

The Most High also says:

“Indeed, Abraham was a leader, devoutly obedient to Allah, inclining to Him alone, and he was not one of the polytheists.”

A “leader” here is a teacher of good whom others follow, just as a “role model” is someone whose example others follow. Allah Most High placed prophethood and Scripture among his descendants, and the prophets He sent after him were sent with his religion. The Most High says:

“Then We revealed to you: Follow the religion of Abraham, inclining to Allah alone; he was not one of the polytheists.”

The Most High also says:

“Indeed, those with the greatest claim to Abraham are those who followed him, this Prophet, and those who believe. And Allah is the protector of the believers.”

The Most High also says:

“Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but one inclining to Allah alone, submitting to Him; he was not one of the polytheists.”

The Most High also says:

“They say: Be Jews or Christians, and you will be guided. Say: Rather, we follow the religion of Abraham, inclining to Allah alone; he was not one of the polytheists.”

“Say: We believe in Allah and in what has been sent down to us and what was sent down to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes”—up to His words—“and to Him we submit.”

It is authentically reported in the Sahīh that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Abraham is the best of creation.”

He is thus the greatest of the prophets after the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he is the intimate friend of Allah Most High.

It is also authentically reported in the Sahīh through several routes that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah has taken me as an intimate friend, just as He took Abraham as an intimate friend.”

He also said:

“If I were to take anyone on earth as an intimate friend, I would take Abū Bakr as an intimate friend. But your companion is Allah’s intimate friend”—meaning himself.

He also said:

“There must not remain

---

## Page 4783

any small doorway in the mosque that is not sealed, except the doorway of Abū Bakr.” He also said:

“Those before you used to take graves as places of worship. Beware: do not take graves as places of worship, for I forbid you to do so.”

All of this is recorded in the Sahīh. It also states that he said this a few days before his death. This was part of completing his mission, for it affirms the perfection of his intimate friendship with Allah, founded upon Allah Most High’s love for His servant and the servant’s love for Allah, contrary to the Jahmiyyah. It also affirms Allah’s oneness and that none but Him should be worshipped, refuting those who resemble the polytheists. It further refutes the Rāfidah, who deny al-Siddīq his due and who, among those who profess allegiance to the qiblah, are the greatest in associating human beings with Allah.

Intimate friendship is perfect love, which entails, on the servant’s part, perfect servitude to Allah and, on the Lord’s part—glory be to Him—perfect lordship over His servants whom He loves and who love Him. The term “servitude” encompasses perfect humility and perfect love. The Arabs describe a heart as mutayyam (enthralled) when it is enslaved to the beloved. Mutayyam means “enslaved,” and Taym Allāh means “Allah’s servant.” Abraham and Muhammad, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace, attained this in its perfection. This is why he had no intimate friend among the people of the earth: intimate friendship admits no sharing. As has been said on this subject:

---

## Page 4784

“You have permeated the very course of my soul;
Thus is an intimate friend called khalīl.”

Love in the broader sense is different. In an authentic hadith, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said concerning al-Hasan and Usāmah:

“O Allah, I love them both, so love them and love those who love them.”

Amr ibn al-Ās asked him, “Who is dearest to you?” He replied, “Ā’ishah.” He asked, “And among men?” He replied, “Her father.”

He also said to Alī, may Allah be pleased with him:

“I shall certainly give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love.”

There are many similar examples. Allah Most High has stated that He loves the God-fearing, those who do good, those who act justly, those who repent, those who purify themselves, and those who fight in His cause in ranks as though they were a solidly joined structure. He also said:

“Allah will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him.”

He has thus affirmed His love for His believing servants and the believers’ love for Him, even saying:

“But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah.”

Intimate friendship, however, is exclusive. Some people say, “Muhammad is Allah’s beloved, whereas Abraham is Allah’s intimate friend,” imagining that love is higher than intimate friendship. This is a weak view, for Muhammad is also Allah’s intimate friend, as established in widely transmitted authentic hadiths. As for the report that “al-Abbās will be gathered at the Resurrection between a beloved and an intimate friend,” and similar reports, these are fabricated hadiths that cannot be relied upon.

---

## Page 4785

We have already explained that loving Allah Most High includes loving what He loves. Thus, in the two Sahīh collections, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever possesses three qualities will taste the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than all else; that he loves another person solely for Allah’s sake; and that he detests returning to disbelief after Allah has rescued him from it just as he detests being cast into the Fire.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stated that whoever possesses these three qualities will taste the sweetness of faith. This is because finding sweetness in something follows love for it. When someone loves or desires something and then obtains what he wants, he experiences sweetness, pleasure, and joy in it. Pleasure arises after perceiving what is congenial—that is, what is loved or desired.

Those who claim that pleasure is the perception of what is congenial, as some philosophers and physicians do, are clearly mistaken. Perception comes between love and pleasure. A person, for example, desires food; when he eats it, pleasure follows. Likewise, pleasure follows looking at something: when one looks at it, one experiences pleasure. Pleasure follows the act of looking; it is not the act of looking itself, nor is it the sight of the thing. Rather, it arises after seeing it. Allah Most High said:

“Therein is whatever souls desire and eyes delight in.”

Likewise, all the pleasures and pains the soul experiences—joy, sorrow, and the like—arise through awareness of what is loved or what is disliked. Yet awareness itself is not

---

## Page 4786

joy or sorrow. The sweetness of faith—with the pleasure and joy experienced by the believer who tastes it—follows from the perfection of the servant’s love for Allah. This involves three things: perfecting this love, extending it, and repelling its opposite.

“Perfecting it” means that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than all else. Merely possessing some love for Allah and His Messenger is insufficient; rather, they must be dearer to him than all else, as explained earlier. “Extending it” means loving another person solely for Allah’s sake. “Repelling its opposite” means detesting the opposite of faith more than being cast into the Fire.

If loving the Messenger and the believers is part of loving Allah, and Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, loves the believers whom Allah loves—because his love for Allah is the most perfect of all people’s, and he is the one most worthy of loving what Allah loves and hating what He hates—yet no one other than Allah has any share in his “intimate friendship,” and he even said:

“Were I to take anyone on earth as an intimate friend, I would take Abū Bakr as an intimate friend,”

then it is clear that intimate friendship holds a higher rank than love in general.

And (the point) is that “intimate friendship” and “love for Allah” fulfil servitude to Him. Those who err in this matter do so only because they imagine that servitude is merely abasement

---

## Page 4787

and submission alone, unaccompanied by love; or that love entails indulgence in desires or an abasement incompatible with lordship. Thus, it is related that when people discussed love in the presence of Dhū al-Nūn, he said:

“Refrain from discussing this matter, lest souls hear of it and claim it for themselves.”

Some people of spiritual insight and knowledge disapproved of keeping company with those who spoke much about love without reverent fear. Some of the early generations said:

“Whoever worships Allah through love alone is a heretic; whoever worships Him through hope alone is a Murji’ite; whoever worships Him through fear alone is a Harūrī (Kharijite); and whoever worships Him through love, fear, and hope is a believer who affirms His oneness.”

Thus, among later generations, some became so unrestrained in their claims of love that this led them into a kind of folly and pretension incompatible with servitude, involving the servant in a kind of lordship befitting Allah alone. One of them makes claims exceeding the bounds of prophets and messengers, or they ask Allah for what belongs exclusively to Allah in every respect and is not fitting even for prophets and messengers. Many spiritual masters have fallen into this.

Its cause is a failure to fully realize the servitude explained by the messengers and precisely defined by the commands and prohibitions they brought—indeed, a weakness of the reason through which the servant recognizes his own true nature. When reason is weak, knowledge of religion is scant, and love is present in the soul, the soul foolishly gives itself free rein in that love, just as someone foolish and ignorant gives himself free rein in loving another person, saying:

“I am a lover, so I am not to be held accountable for the various things I do that involve transgression and ignorance.”

This is

---

## Page 4788

sheer misguidance. It resembles the claim of the Jews and Christians:

“We are the children of Allah and His beloved.”

Allah Most High said:

“Say, ‘Why then does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are human beings among those He has created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills.’”

His punishing them for their sins entails that they are neither beloved nor related to Him as children; rather, they are created beings subject to His lordship. When Allah loves someone, He sets him to doing what his Beloved loves; that person does not commit the disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience that the True One hates and is displeased with. Whoever commits major sins, persists in them, and does not repent of them—Allah hates those deeds of his, just as He loves the good that he does. For His love for a servant is proportionate to that servant’s faith and mindfulness of Him.

Anyone who thinks that sins will not harm him because Allah loves him, despite his persistence in them, is like someone who claims that taking poison will not harm him because he has a healthy constitution, even though he continues taking it and seeks no treatment for it. If this fool reflected on the accounts Allah relates in His Book concerning His prophets—their repentance and seeking forgiveness, and the various trials that befell them, through which they were refined and purified according to their circumstances—he would understand something of the harm sins cause those who commit them, even those of the highest standing.

Someone who loves a created being but neither knows nor seeks that being’s best interests, acting instead merely on the impulse of love—even when this involves ignorance and wrongdoing—thereby gives the beloved cause to hate him and turn away from him, indeed, even to punish him.

---

## Page 4789

Many seekers on the spiritual path, in professing love for Allah, have pursued various courses born of ignorance of religion: transgressing Allah’s limits, neglecting His rights, or making groundless claims with no basis in reality. One of them said:

“I disown any disciple of mine who leaves anyone in the Fire.”

Another said:

“I disown any disciple of mine who allows any believer to enter the Fire.”

The first credited his disciple with bringing everyone out of the Fire; the second credited his disciple with preventing those guilty of major sins from entering it. Some of them say:

“On the Day of Resurrection, I shall pitch my tent over Hell so that no one enters it.”

Such statements, and others like them, are reported from certain well-known spiritual masters. They are either falsely attributed to them or errors on their part. Such words may be uttered in a state of spiritual intoxication, overpowering emotion, and loss of self-awareness, in which a person’s discernment disappears or becomes so impaired that he does not know what he has said. “Intoxication” is pleasure accompanied by a lack of discernment. Thus, some among them would seek forgiveness for such words upon recovering their sobriety. This was the principal aim of those masters who indulged extensively in listening to poems of love, longing, blame, reproach, and consuming passion.

For this reason, Allah revealed a test of love by which He tests the one who professes it. He said:

“Say, ‘If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you.’”

No one truly loves Allah unless he follows His Messenger. Obeying and following the Messenger brings true servitude to Allah into being. Yet many who profess love depart from his law and Sunnah and make claims involving

---

## Page 4790

fantasies that there is no room to recount here. One of them may even imagine that he is no longer bound by divine commands, that forbidden things have become lawful for him, and other notions contrary to the Messenger’s law and Sunnah and to obedience to him. Yet Allah has made jihad in His cause an expression of love for Him and His Messenger. “Jihad” entails complete love for what Allah has commanded and complete hatred of what He has forbidden. Thus, describing those whom He loves and who love Him, He says:

“Humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers, striving in Allah’s cause.”

For this reason, this community’s love for Allah is more complete than that of earlier communities, and their servitude to Allah is more complete than that of their predecessors. The most perfect members of this community in this respect are the Companions of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. The more closely someone resembles them, the more complete these qualities are in him. How far removed this is from people who merely profess love!

Among the sayings of certain spiritual masters is:

“Love is a fire that burns away from the heart everything other than what the Beloved wills.”

They meant that Allah has willed the existence of the entire universe, and so they supposed that perfect love requires the servant to love everything—even disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience. Yet no one can love everything that exists. Rather, a person loves what suits and benefits him, and hates what is incompatible with him and harms him. Through this error, however, they found a means of following their own desires. They love whatever they desire, such as physical forms, leadership, surplus wealth, and misleading innovations, claiming that this is part of loving Allah. Yet loving Allah includes hating what Allah and His Messenger hate, and waging jihad against those who engage in it with one’s life and wealth.

---

## Page 4791

Their fundamental error is that the person who said,

“Love is a fire that burns away everything other than what the Beloved wills,”

meant by Allah’s will His religious, legislative will, which signifies His love and pleasure. It is as though he had said, “It burns away from the heart everything other than what Allah loves.” This meaning is sound. Perfect love entails loving only what Allah loves; if you love what He does not love, your love is deficient. As for His decreeing and ordaining such a thing, He hates and detests it, is angered by it, and forbids it. If I do not share His hatred, aversion, and anger toward it, then I do not love Him; rather, I love what He hates.

Following the revealed law and undertaking jihad are therefore among the greatest distinctions between those who love Allah and His allies, whom He loves and who love Him, and those who claim to love Allah while considering only His all-encompassing lordship or following innovations contrary to His law. Such claims to love Allah are of the same kind as the claims of Jews and Christians to love Him. Indeed, these people’s claims may be worse than those of Jews and Christians because of their hypocrisy, which places them in the lowest depths of the Fire. Conversely, the claims of Jews and Christians may be worse than theirs if these people have not reached the same degree of disbelief. The Torah and the Gospel contain teachings about loving Allah on which they agree; indeed, they regard this as the greatest commandment of the Law.

Thus, the Gospel relates that the Messiah said:

“The greatest of the Messiah’s commandments is to love Allah with all your heart, mind, and soul.”

Christians claim that they fulfil this love and that their asceticism and worship are expressions of it. Yet they are devoid of love for Allah, since they did not

---

## Page 4792

follow what He loved. Rather, they followed what angered Allah and disliked His pleasure, so He rendered their deeds worthless. Allah hates the disbelievers, detests them, and curses them. He, glorified is He, loves those who love Him. A servant cannot love Allah without Allah Most High loving him. Rather, Allah’s love for His servant corresponds to the servant’s love for his Lord, although Allah’s reward for His servant is greater.

As Allah Most High says in the authentic divine hadith:

“Whoever draws near to Me a handspan, I draw near to him an arm’s length. Whoever draws near to Me an arm’s length, I draw near to him an armspan. Whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running.”

He, glorified is He, has declared that He loves the God-fearing, those who do good, the patient, those who repeatedly repent, and those who purify themselves. Indeed, He loves whoever fulfils His commands, whether obligatory or recommended, as stated in the authentic hadith:

“My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him. When I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears and his sight with which he sees”—to the end of the hadith.

Many of those who have erred by following spiritual teachers in “asceticism and worship” have fallen into some of the same errors as the Christians: claiming to love Allah while violating His law, neglecting to strive in His cause, and the like. In the religion through which they seek to draw near to Allah, they cling to things similar to those to which the Christians clung: ambiguous statements and accounts whose tellers’ truthfulness is unknown. Even if a teller were truthful, he would not be infallible. Thus they make those whom they follow into lawgivers who prescribe a religion for them, just as the Christians made their priests and monks lawgivers

---

## Page 4793

who prescribed a religion for them. They then disparage servitude to Allah and claim that the spiritual elite transcend it, just as the Christians claim concerning the Messiah. They attribute to this elite a share in divinity of the same kind that the Christians attribute to the Messiah and his mother. There are other such errors whose explanation would be too lengthy here.

The true religion consists only in fully realizing servitude to Allah in every respect, which means fully realizing love for Allah at every degree. As servitude becomes more complete, so too does the servant’s love for his Lord and the Lord’s love for His servant. As the former diminishes, so does the latter. Whenever the heart contains love for something other than Allah, it contains a corresponding degree of servitude to something other than Allah; and whenever it contains servitude to something other than Allah, it contains a corresponding degree of love for something other than Allah. Every love that is not for Allah’s sake is vain, and every deed through which Allah’s Face is not sought is vain. This world is accursed, and everything in it is accursed, except what is for Allah. Nothing is for Allah unless Allah and His Messenger love it—that is, unless it is prescribed in His religion.

Thus, any deed intended for someone other than Allah is not for Allah, and any deed that does not conform to Allah’s law is not for Allah. Rather, nothing is for Allah unless it combines both qualities: it must be for Allah’s sake, and it must accord with what Allah and His Messenger love—namely, what is obligatory or recommended.

As He says:

“So whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and associate no one in the worship of his Lord.”

Righteous deeds—those that are obligatory or recommended—are therefore indispensable, and they must be devoted sincerely to seeking the Face of Allah Most High. As He, Most High, says:

“Yes, whoever submits himself to Allah while doing good will have his reward with his Lord. No fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.”

And there are the words of

---

## Page 4794

the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Whoever performs a deed that does not accord with our command, it is rejected.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also said:

“Actions are judged only by intentions, and each person will have only what he intended. Whoever migrates for Allah and His Messenger, his migration is for Allah and His Messenger. But whoever migrates for some worldly gain or to marry a woman, his migration is for whatever he migrated for.”

This principle is the foundation of religion, and religion is fully realized to the extent that this principle is fulfilled. Allah sent the messengers and revealed the Books with it. The Messenger called people to it and strove for it; he enjoined it and encouraged people to embrace it. It is the central axis around which religion revolves.

Associating partners with Allah is prevalent among human souls. As stated in the hadith:

“Among this community, it is more imperceptible than the creeping of ants.”

Another hadith relates:

“Abū Bakr said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, how can we escape it when it is more imperceptible than the creeping of ants?’

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to Abū Bakr, ‘Shall I not teach you words which, if you say them, will save you from it, small and great? Say: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowingly associating partners with You, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do unknowingly.”’”

ʿUmar used to say in his supplication:

“O Allah, make all my deeds righteous, make them sincerely devoted to seeking Your Face, and let no one else have any share in them.”

Hidden desires often mingle with human souls, undermining their full realization of

---

## Page 4795

their love for Allah, their servitude to Him, and their sincere religious devotion to Him alone. As Shaddād ibn Aws said:

“O remnant of the Arabs, what I fear most for you is showing off and hidden desire.”

Abū Dāwūd al-Sijistānī was asked, “What is hidden desire?” He replied, “Love of leadership.”

Kaʿb ibn Mālik reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Two hungry wolves let loose in a sheepfold are no more destructive to it than a person’s eagerness for wealth and prestige is to his religion.”

Al-Tirmidhī said, “A good and authentic hadith.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thus explained that eagerness for wealth and prestige is no less destructive to religion than two hungry wolves are to a sheepfold. This is clear, for sound religious devotion does not harbour such eagerness. Once the heart tastes the sweetness of servitude to Allah and love for Him, nothing becomes dearer to it such that it would give it precedence over that. Through this, evil and indecency are turned away from those sincerely devoted to Allah, as the Most High said:

“Thus it was, so that We might turn evil and indecency away from him. Indeed, he was one of Our chosen servants.”

One who is sincerely devoted to Allah has tasted a sweetness in serving Him that prevents him from serving anyone else, and a sweetness in loving Him that prevents him from loving anyone else. For the heart finds nothing sweeter, more delightful, more pleasant, gentler or more blissful than the sweetness of faith, which encompasses servitude to Allah, love for Him, and sincere religious devotion to Him alone. This draws the heart towards Allah, so that it turns to Him in repentance, fearing Him, filled with longing and awe. As the Most High said:

“One who feared the Most Merciful without seeing Him and came with a heart ever turning to Him.”

For one who loves fears losing what he seeks and the occurrence of

---

## Page 4796

what he desires. Thus, one can only be a servant of Allah and love Him while living between fear and hope. The Most High said:

“Those whom they invoke seek a means of nearness to their Lord, striving to be closest to Him. They hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, your Lord’s punishment is ever to be feared.”

When a servant is sincerely devoted to Him, his Lord chooses him, revives his heart and draws him towards Himself. The evil and indecency that oppose this are thereby turned away from him, and he fears that the opposite might befall him. By contrast, a heart that is not sincerely devoted to Allah pursues, desires and loves without restraint. It craves whatever presents itself and clings to whatever it desires, like a branch that bends with every passing breeze.

At times, he is drawn to physical beauty, whether forbidden to him or not, and remains a captive and a slave to someone whom it would be shameful, demeaning and blameworthy for him to take as his own slave. At other times, he is drawn to prestige and leadership: a word pleases him, and a word angers him. Whoever praises him enslaves him, even through falsehood, while he becomes hostile towards whoever criticizes him, even truthfully. At still other times, he is enslaved by silver and gold, and by other such things that enslave hearts and that hearts desire. Thus he takes his own desire as his god and follows it without guidance from Allah.

Unless a person is sincerely devoted to Allah as His servant, with his heart wholly enslaved to his Lord alone, without partner—so that Allah is dearer to him than everything else, and he is humble and submissive before Him—created things will enslave him, and devils will take possession of his heart. He will be among the misguided, the brethren of the devils, and evil and indecency will arise within him to an extent known only to Allah. This is inevitable; there is no escaping it. For if the heart is not devoted to Allah alone, turning towards Him and turning away from whatever

---

## Page 4797

is other than Him, it will instead associate partners with Him. The Most High said:

“So set your face towards the religion, inclining to truth—the natural disposition Allah has instilled in mankind. There is no altering Allah’s creation. That is the upright religion, but most people do not know.”

Up to His words:

“Each faction rejoicing in what it has.”

Allah, glorified is He, made Abraham and the family of Abraham leaders of these sincere monotheists, who love Allah, worship Him and devote their religion sincerely to Him. Likewise, He made Pharaoh and the people of Pharaoh leaders of those who associate partners with Allah and follow their own desires.

The Most High said concerning Abraham:

“And We granted him Isaac, and Jacob as an additional gift, and made them all righteous.”

“And We made them leaders, guiding by Our command, and inspired them to do good deeds, establish prayer and give zakah. And they worshipped Us alone.”

He said concerning Pharaoh and his people:

“And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.”

“And We caused a curse to follow them in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised.”

Thus, the followers of Pharaoh first come to make no distinction between what Allah loves and approves of and what He has decreed and ordained. Rather, they consider only His unrestricted, all-encompassing will. Eventually, they cease to distinguish between the Creator and creation, regarding the existence of the one as the very existence of the other. [Their leading exponents say: “In the revealed Law there is obedience and disobedience, while in spiritual reality there is disobedience without obedience”]; at the level of realization, there is neither obedience nor disobedience. This is the full realization of the doctrine of Pharaoh and his people, who denied the Creator, denied that He spoke to His servant Moses, and denied the commands and prohibitions with which He sent him.
