## Page 5005

The Shaykh—may Allah have mercy on him—said:

Section

As for his question, “Is seclusion or mixing with others better for someone following the spiritual path?”—although people dispute this “question,” either in general terms or with reference to particular circumstances, the truth is that “mixing with others” is sometimes obligatory or recommended. The same person may be instructed to mix with others at one time and to remain alone at another.

The governing principle is this: if “associating with others” involves cooperation in righteousness and piety, it is enjoined; if it involves cooperation in sin and transgression, it is forbidden. Thus, joining Muslims in acts of worship—such as the five daily prayers, Friday prayer, the two Eid prayers, the eclipse prayer, the prayer for rain, and similar acts—is among the things Allah and His Messenger have commanded. The same applies to joining them in Hajj and in military expeditions against the disbelievers and the renegade Khawārij, even if those leading these activities are wicked, and even if there are wicked people among those assembled.

---

## Page 5006

and likewise to gatherings through which a servant’s faith increases—whether by receiving benefit or benefiting others, and the like.

A servant must also have times alone for supplication, remembrance of Allah, prayer, reflection, self-examination, setting his heart right, and attending to personal matters in which no one else shares. These require solitude, whether at home—as Tāwūs said, “What an excellent hermitage a man’s home is: there he restrains his gaze and his tongue”—or elsewhere. To favour mixing with others unconditionally is therefore mistaken, as is favouring solitude unconditionally. How much each person needs of either, and what is best for him in each circumstance, requires individual consideration, as explained earlier.

The same applies to “taking practical means and foregoing them.” Whoever is able to take such means without being distracted from what is more beneficial to his religion is commanded to do so while placing his trust in Allah. This is better for him than accepting from others, even if something comes to him without his asking. For such a person, taking these means is an act of worship of Allah, and he is commanded to worship Allah and put his trust in Him. If, however, he takes these means without a righteous intention, or does not put his trust in Allah, then he is [not] (1) obedient in these two respects, and this is [not] (2) the way of the prophets and the Companions. As for someone among the poor who are restricted in Allah’s cause and are unable to

## Page 5007

travel through the land, and whom the uninformed consider wealthy because they refrain from asking—such a person is either unable to earn a living or able to do so at the cost of an activity in which he is more obedient to Allah than he would be by earning a living. Pursuing the activity in which he is more obedient is what is prescribed for him. This varies according to people’s circumstances.

As explained earlier, what is best varies “sometimes” according to the category of worship: prayer as a category is better than Quran recitation, Quran recitation is better than remembrance of Allah, and remembrance of Allah is better than supplication.

“Sometimes” it varies according to the time: after Fajr and Asr, Quran recitation, remembrance of Allah, and supplication are prescribed rather than prayer.

“Sometimes” it varies according to the outward act a person is performing: during bowing and prostration, remembrance of Allah and supplication are prescribed rather than Quran recitation. Likewise, remembrance of Allah and supplication during circumambulation are prescribed by scholarly agreement, whereas Quran recitation during circumambulation is a matter of well-known disagreement.

“Sometimes” it varies according to the place: at Arafah, Muzdalifah, the stoning sites, and Safā and Marwah, remembrance of Allah and supplication are prescribed rather than prayer and similar acts. For someone arriving in Mecca, circumambulating the House is better than prayer, whereas for residents of Mecca, prayer is better.

---

## Page 5008

And “sometimes” it varies according to the rank of a given category of worship: for men, jihad is better than Hajj, whereas for women, their jihad is Hajj. For a married woman, obedience to her husband takes precedence over obedience to her parents, unlike an unmarried woman, who is commanded to obey her parents.

“Sometimes” it varies according to a person’s ability or inability: the acts of worship he can perform are better for him than those he cannot, even if the latter belong to a superior category. This is a broad subject in which many people go to extremes and follow their desires. Some people find that a particular deed is better for them because it suits them, benefits their hearts more, and helps them obey their Lord more fully; they then want to make it the best deed for everyone and instruct others to do likewise.

Allah sent Muhammad with the Book and wisdom, making him a mercy and a guide to His servants, instructing each person to do what is best for him. A Muslim must therefore sincerely seek the good of fellow Muslims, desiring for each person what is best for him.

This makes it clear to you that, for some people, the voluntary pursuit of knowledge is best; for others, voluntary jihad is best; and for others, voluntary acts of worship

---

## Page 5009

performed with the body—such as prayer and fasting—are best for them. What is best overall is that which most closely resembles the Prophet’s way, both inwardly and outwardly—may Allah bless him and grant him peace. For the best speech is Allah’s speech, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace. And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows best.

## Page 5010

The shaykh also said:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. May Allah bless him and grant him abundant peace.

To proceed:

Know that every sane adult, whether human or jinn, must bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. He sent him with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all other religions, and sufficient is Allah as a witness.

He sent him to all creation: humans and jinn, Arabs and non-Arabs, Persians, Indians, Berbers, Romans, and all other non-Arab peoples, black and white. By non-Arabs is meant those who are not Arabs, whatever their languages.

Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—was sent to everyone among humans and jinn, whether People of the Book or otherwise, concerning every inward and outward matter of religion: its beliefs, realities, paths, and laws. There is no creed but his creed, no reality but his reality, no path but his path, and no religious law but his religious law. No created being can reach Allah or attain His good pleasure, His Paradise, or the honor He bestows

---

## Page 5011

and His friendship except by following him inwardly and outwardly in words and deeds: in the heart’s affirmations and beliefs, its states and realities, the speech of the tongue, and the actions of the limbs. No one is a close friend of Allah unless he follows him inwardly and outwardly, believing what he has reported about the unseen and committing himself to obeying him in what he has enjoined upon creation: fulfilling obligations and abstaining from prohibitions.

Whoever does not believe what he has reported and commit himself to obeying what he has made obligatory and commanded, both in the inward matters of the heart and in outward bodily actions, is not a believer, let alone a close friend of Allah, however extraordinary the feats he may perform. If he neglects to do what is commanded and to abstain from what is forbidden—including fulfilling obligations such as prayer and other duties, with their requisite purification and obligatory elements—then his states can only be satanic states, which distance him from Allah and bring him nearer to His wrath and punishment.

As for children and the insane who are not religiously accountable, the pen of accountability has been lifted from them, so they are not punished. They do not possess the inward and outward faith in Allah and piety that would place them among Allah’s pious close friends, His successful party, and His victorious forces. They are, however, included within Islam by virtue of their parents’ affiliation, as the Most High says:

“And those who believe and whose descendants follow them in faith—We will join their descendants with them, without diminishing the reward of their deeds in any way. Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned.”

---

## Page 5012

Yet, lacking reason, they cannot be among those whose hearts possess the realities of faith, the knowledge of Allah’s close friends, and the spiritual states of His chosen servants, for all these things depend upon reason. Insanity is incompatible with reason, assent, knowledge, certainty, guidance, and praise. Allah raises in rank only those who believe and those who have been given knowledge. Thus, although Allah does not punish the insane person and shows him mercy in the Hereafter, he is not among Allah’s close friends—those brought near to Him and those who follow a middle course—whose ranks Allah raises.

Whoever believes that any of these people who neither fulfil their obligations nor abstain from prohibitions—whether sane, insane, bereft of their senses, or lost in bewilderment—is among Allah’s pious close friends, His successful party, His righteous servants, His victorious forces, the foremost who are brought near to Him, and those who follow a middle course, whose ranks Allah raises through knowledge and faith, despite that person neither fulfilling his obligations nor abstaining from prohibitions: whoever believes such a person to be a close friend of Allah is a disbeliever who has apostatized from Islam. He does not bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; rather, he denies what Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has testified to.

For Muhammad reported from Allah that Allah’s close friends are the pious believers. The Most High says:

“Indeed, the close friends of Allah will have no fear, nor will they grieve—”

“Those who believed and were mindful of Allah.”

And the Most High says:

“O mankind, We created you from a male and a female and made you into peoples and tribes so that you may know one another. Indeed, the most honourable of you in Allah’s sight is the most pious of you.”

---

## Page 5013

And “piety” means obeying Allah, guided by light from Allah and hoping for His mercy, and refraining from disobedience to Allah, guided by light from Allah and fearing His punishment. A close friend of Allah draws near to Him only by fulfilling the obligatory duties, then performing voluntary acts of worship. Allah Most High says:

“My servant has not drawn near to Me through anything like fulfilling what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him.”

This is related in the authentic divine hadith narrated by al-Bukhārī.

Section

Among the deeds most beloved to Allah and the greatest obligations in His sight are the five daily prayers at their prescribed times. They are the first deeds for which a servant will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection. Allah Most High Himself made them obligatory on the night of the Ascension, placing no intermediary between Himself and Muhammad in this matter. Prayer is the pillar of Islam, without which it cannot stand, and the most important matter of religion. As the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb, used to write to his officials:

“The most important of your affairs in my eyes is prayer. Whoever observes it and maintains it faithfully preserves his religion. Whoever neglects it will neglect his other deeds even more.”

It is authentically reported in the Sahīh that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Between a servant and associating partners with Allah lies the abandonment of prayer.”

He also said: “The covenant between us and them

---

## Page 5014

is prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved.”

Whoever does not believe that prayer is obligatory upon every sane person who has reached puberty, except women who are menstruating or experiencing postnatal bleeding, is a disbeliever and an apostate, by agreement of the leading scholars of the Muslims. Even if he believes that it is a righteous deed which Allah loves and rewards, and he himself prays, stands in prayer at night, and fasts during the day, yet does not believe it obligatory upon everyone who has reached puberty, he is likewise a disbeliever and an apostate until he believes that it is a binding obligation upon every sane person who has reached puberty.

Whoever believes that this obligation is waived for certain shaykhs who possess spiritual knowledge, receive unveilings, and have attained their goal; or that Allah has an elect upon whom prayer is not obligatory, but from whom its obligation has been lifted because they have reached the Sacred Presence, or because something more important or more worthy renders them independent of it; or that the purpose is for the heart to be present with the Lord; or that prayer disperses one's attention, so that when a servant is wholly concentrated upon Allah, he has no need of prayer—rather, the purpose of prayer is spiritual knowledge, and once that is attained, he no longer needs prayer, for the aim is for you to perform an extraordinary feat, such as flying through the air, walking on water, filling vessels with water from the air, making waters sink away and extracting the treasures beneath them, or killing someone he hates through satanic states, so that once he achieves this, he has no further need of prayer—and other such notions; or that Allah has certain members of His elect who do not need to follow Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, but have become independent of him just as al-Khidr was independent of Moses; or that every

---

## Page 5015

person who receives unveilings and flies through the air or walks on water is a friend of Allah, whether he prays or not; or believes that prayer is accepted without ritual purification; or regards as friends of Allah the ecstatics, the enraptured, and the insane who frequent cemeteries, rubbish dumps, tahārāt, inns, qamāmīn, and other such places, neither performing ablution nor offering the obligatory prayers—whoever believes that these people are friends of Allah is a disbeliever and an apostate from Islam, by agreement of the leading scholars of Islam, even if he himself is an ascetic devoted to worship.

Monks are even more ascetic and devoted to worship. They believe in much of what the Messenger brought, and most of them revere the Messenger and his followers. Yet they have not believed in everything he brought; rather, they have believed in some and disbelieved in some, thereby becoming disbelievers. As Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to distinguish between Allah and His messengers, saying, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others,’ and wish to adopt a way in between—

“Those are the disbelievers, truly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.

“But those who believe in Allah and His messengers and make no distinction between any of them—to those He will give their rewards. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.”

As for someone deprived of reason or insane, the most that can be said is that he is exempt from accountability and therefore incurs no punishment. His faith, prayer, fasting, and all his other deeds are invalid, for no deeds are accepted without reason. Thus, anyone who lacks reason

---

## Page 5016

has no valid acts of worship, whether obligatory or voluntary. Whoever has neither obligatory nor voluntary acts of worship is not among the friends of Allah.

For this reason, Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, in that are signs for those of understanding.”

That is, those who possess reason. Allah Most High also says:

“Is there not in this an oath sufficient for a person of understanding?”

That is, a person of reason. Allah Most High says:

“And fear Me, O people of understanding.”

He also says:

“Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason.”

And Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Quran so that you may understand.”

Allah praises and commends only those who possess reason. As for those who lack reason, Allah has neither praised nor commended them, nor has He ever spoken favourably of them. Rather, Allah Most High says of the people of the Fire:

“And they will say, ‘If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, eyes with which they do not see, and ears with which they do not hear. They are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. It is they who are heedless.”

And He says:

“Or do you think that most of them hear or reason? They are only like livestock; rather, they are even further astray.”

Thus, anyone who lacks reason has neither valid faith nor valid obligatory or voluntary worship. If someone was a Jew or a Christian, then became insane and embraced Islam after becoming insane, his acceptance of Islam is valid neither inwardly nor outwardly. If someone had believed, then disbelieved and subsequently became insane, he is subject to the same ruling as disbelievers. Whoever was a believer and subsequently became insane will be rewarded for the faith he had during

---

## Page 5017

his sanity. Whoever was born insane and remained so can have neither valid faith nor valid disbelief. An insane person is subject to the same ruling as a child: if both his parents are Muslims, he is considered a Muslim by virtue of his parents, by agreement of the Muslims. The same applies if his mother is Muslim, according to the majority of scholars, including Abū Hanīfah, al-Shāfiʿī and Ahmad. Likewise, those who become insane after embracing Islam retain Muslim status by virtue of their fathers. An insane person born among Muslims is also outwardly considered a Muslim by virtue of his parents or the inhabitants of the land, just as children are—not because of any faith within him. The children and the insane among Muslims will follow their fathers on the Day of Resurrection. This Muslim status neither gives such a person any distinction over others nor makes him one of Allah’s pious friends who draw near to Him through obligatory and voluntary acts of worship.

Allah Most High says:

“O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying, nor in a state of major ritual impurity—except when passing through—until you have washed yourselves.”

Allah, Almighty and Majestic, thus forbade them to approach prayer while intoxicated until they knew what they were saying. By agreement of the scholars, this verse was revealed before wine was prohibited by the verse Allah revealed in Surah al-Mā’idah.

It has been reported that the occasion of its revelation was that one of the Companions led his companions in prayer after drinking wine, before it was prohibited, and became confused in his recitation. Allah then revealed this verse. Thus, if Allah forbade prayer while intoxicated, even when the drinking itself had not been prohibited, until people knew what they were saying, it follows that prayer must not be performed

---

## Page 5018

by anyone until he knows what he is saying. Whoever does not know what he is saying is not permitted to pray, even if he has lost his reason through something that is not forbidden. Hence, the scholars agree that the prayer of someone who has lost his reason is invalid, whatever the cause. How much more, then, does this apply to an insane person!

Some Quran commentators have said—and this is reported from al-Dahhāk—“Do not approach prayer while you are stupefied with sleep.” This interpretation holds if the verse is understood to indicate this by inference or through the inclusive meaning of its general wording. Otherwise, there is no doubt that the occasion of the verse’s revelation concerned intoxication from wine, and its wording explicitly indicates that. The other meaning is also sound.

It is authentically reported in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When one of you rises to pray at night and his tongue falters in reciting the Quran, let him sleep, for he does not know: he may intend to seek forgiveness but instead curse himself.” In another wording: “If he rises to pray and becomes drowsy, let him sleep.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thus forbade praying when drowsiness causes a person to make mistakes. The scholars have cited this as evidence that drowsiness does not invalidate ablution. Were ablution invalidated by it, the prayer would become invalid, or one would have to leave it to renew one’s ritual purification. Yet the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explained the reason only by saying:

“For he does not know: he may intend to seek forgiveness but instead curse himself.”

It is therefore clear that he intended to forbid prayer for someone who does not know what he is saying, even when this is caused by drowsiness.

In keeping with this, it is authentically reported from him in the Sahīh that he said:

“Prayer must not be performed by

---

## Page 5019

any of you while resisting the urge to urinate or defecate, or when food is present.” This is because such things distract the heart.

Abū al-Dardā’ said:

“A sign of a man’s understanding is that he first attends to his needs, then turns to his prayer with an unoccupied heart.”

If prayer is forbidden whenever a person is deprived of reason—even through something permissible—until he knows what he is saying, then it is all the more clearly impermissible for an insane person to pray, or anyone who falls within that designation, even if described as distraught or bewildered.

It is well known that prayer is “the finest act of worship,” as reported in the two Sahīh collections from Ibn Masʿūd, who said:

“I asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ‘Which deed is most beloved to Allah?’

“He replied, ‘Prayer at its appointed time.’

“I asked, ‘Then which?’

“He replied, ‘Dutifulness to one’s parents.’

“I asked, ‘Then which?’

“He replied, ‘Striving in Allah’s cause.’”

Ibn Masʿūd said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, told me these things, and had I asked him for more, he would have told me more.”

It is also authentically reported in the two Sahīh collections that he ranked faith in Allah and striving in His cause as the best deeds, followed by an accepted Hajj.

There is no contradiction between the two reports, for prayer is included within the meaning of faith in Allah, just as it is included in His words, Most High:

“Allah would never let your faith go to waste.”

Al-Barā’ ibn ʿĀzib and others among the early generations said: “That is, your prayers facing Jerusalem.”

For this reason, prayer, like faith, cannot under any circumstances be performed on another’s behalf. No one may perform another person’s obligatory prayer, whether there is an excuse or not, just as no one can have faith on another’s behalf; nor

---

## Page 5020

does its obligation ever lapse, just as the obligation of faith does not lapse. Rather, he must pray as long as his reason remains intact and he can perform some of its actions. If he is incapable of performing any of its actions and cannot utter its words, should he pray by moving his eyes and mentally recalling its actions? Scholars hold two views on this, though the stronger view is that this is not prescribed.

Thus, it becomes clear that someone who has lost his reason has been deprived of the obligatory and voluntary acts through which he might draw near to Allah. “Friendship with Allah” consists of faith and piety, which entail drawing near to Him through obligatory and voluntary acts. He has therefore been deprived of the means by which Allah’s friends draw near to Him. Nevertheless, while insane, he is exempt from accountability and is not punished, just as children and animals are not punished, since they bear no religious responsibility in this condition.

If, before the onset of insanity, he was a believer who performed righteous deeds and drew near to Allah through obligatory and voluntary acts, he retains the reward for that previous faith and righteous conduct. His share of friendship with Allah Most High remains commensurate with the faith and piety he possessed, just as this is not lost through death. This differs from apostasy from Islam, for apostasy nullifies deeds. No sin other than apostasy nullifies righteous deeds, just as no good deed other than repentance wipes out all sins.

During his insanity, however, he is not credited with the equivalent of the deeds he used to perform when lucid, just as no equivalent of his previous misdeeds is recorded against him when his reason is absent through intoxicating practices or sleep. This is because, in this condition, he has no sound intention. However, in the hadith

---

## Page 5021

which is authentic and narrated by Abū Mūsā, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When a servant falls ill or travels, he is credited with the deeds he used to perform while healthy and resident.”

It is also authentically reported that during the expedition to Tabūk, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“There are men in Medina who have been with you on every journey you have made and in every valley you have crossed.” They asked, “Even though they are in Medina?” He replied, “Even though they are in Medina. A valid excuse has kept them back.”

These people intended and wished to continue the deeds they used to perform, but were unable to do so. They therefore attained the same standing as those who performed them. This differs from someone who has lost his reason, for he has neither a sound intention nor any worship at all, whereas those people have a sound intention for which reward is recorded.

If, however, before becoming insane, he was a disbeliever, openly disobedient, or sinful, the onset of insanity does not erase his previously established disbelief and disobedience. Thus, Jews and Christians who become insane after embracing Judaism or Christianity will be gathered with their respective communities. Likewise, Muslims who become insane after having faith and piety will be gathered with the pious believers.

Losing one’s reason through insanity or otherwise—whether the person is described as overwhelmed or bewildered—does not increase one’s faith or piety. Nor does the loss of reason cause any increase in one’s goodness, righteousness, or sin. Rather, insanity deprives a person of reason, leaving him with whatever good and evil he already possessed, neither increasing nor diminishing it. His insanity, however, deprives him of further good, just as it prevents him from being punished for evil.

---

## Page 5022

If, however, a person loses his reason through something forbidden—such as drinking wine or consuming hashish, attending melodious singing and listening until he loses his reason, engaging in innovated acts of worship until some devils attach themselves to him and impair his reason, or taking henbane that deprives him of reason—such people deserve blame and punishment for what they have done to deprive themselves of reason.

Many of these people induce a satanic state by doing what pleases them: dancing wildly until they lose their reason, or snorting and bellowing until the satanic state comes upon them. Many deliberately seek bewilderment until they become deranged. All these people belong to Satan’s party, and such conduct is known of more than one of them.

The scholars have disagreed over whether they remain “subject to religious obligations” while deprived of reason. The underlying issue is “the case of an intoxicated person.” The explicitly transmitted position of al-Shāfi‘ī, Ahmad, and others is that such a person remains subject to religious obligations while deprived of reason. Many scholars, however, hold that he is not; this is one of the two positions within the schools of al-Shāfi‘ī and Ahmad. One of the two reports from Ahmad also holds that a divorce pronounced by an intoxicated person does not take effect. This is the stronger of the two views.

None of the scholars has said that those who lose their reason through such means thereby become Allah’s close allies, devoted to His oneness, or members of His successful party. As for those among the ‘wise madmen’ whom the scholars have mentioned favorably, they belong to the first category: those who possessed goodness before losing their reason.

---

## Page 5023

Among the “signs of such people” is that, if they experience some lucidity during their madness, they speak of the faith in their hearts, not disbelief and falsehood. This contrasts with others who, upon regaining some awareness, speak words of disbelief and association of partners with Allah, and babble words of disbelief while deprived of reason. Such a person is a disbeliever, not a Muslim.

As for those who babble unintelligibly in Persian, Turkish, Berber, or other languages—as happens to some who attend gatherings for devotional singing and experience an ecstasy that overwhelms their reason until they babble unintelligibly, or speak in a language other than Arabic—it is Satan who speaks through their tongues, just as he speaks through the tongue of someone possessed.

If someone says that Allah gave these people reason and spiritual states, then preserved their states while taking away their reason, and relieved them of the obligations He had imposed upon them because of what He took away, the response is:

Your statement, “Allah bestowed spiritual states upon them,” is ambiguous. Such states fall into two categories: states from the Most Merciful and satanic states. Whatever extraordinary phenomena these people experience, such as disclosures of hidden matters and astonishing powers of action, may “at times” be of the same kind as those experienced by sorcerers and soothsayers, and “at other times” come from the Most Merciful, like those experienced by people of piety and faith.

If, while in possession of their reason, these people had gifts arising from faith and were pious believers, then there is no doubt that, upon losing their reason, they are relieved of religious obligations because their reason has been taken away. But if what they were given consisted of satanic states—such as those granted to polytheists, the People of the Book, and hypocrites—then losing their reason does not remove them from their previous disbelief and wickedness, just as the former are not removed from their previous faith

---

## Page 5024

and piety. Likewise, for anyone in either group, sleep, death, or unconsciousness does not, through the loss of reason, alter the standing established by his previous faith and obedience or disbelief and wickedness. At most, it removes religious obligations.

Exemption from accountability entails neither praise nor commendation nor reward. Losing his reason does not earn a person any gift bestowed upon Allah’s friends or any miraculous favor granted to the righteous. Rather, he is simply exempted from accountability, just as someone asleep, unconscious, or dead is exempted. There is neither praise nor blame in this. Indeed, someone asleep is in a better condition than these people. Thus, the prophets, peace be upon them, slept, but none of them was insane or mentally deranged. Sleep and unconsciousness can occur to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, but insanity cannot. Our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would sleep with his eyes while his heart remained awake, and he lost consciousness during his illness.

As for “insanity,” Allah has kept His prophets free of it, for it is among the gravest human deficiencies: human perfection lies in reason. This is why Allah has forbidden impairing reason by any means and has forbidden whatever leads to its impairment, such as drinking wine. He has forbidden even a drop of it, although it does not impair reason, because it leads to drinking a large quantity that does impair it. How, then, could losing one’s reason be a cause of friendship with Allah, a condition for it, or something that brings one closer to it, as many misguided people imagine—so much so that one of them said of these people:

---

## Page 5025

“They are a people who have cast off order and breached … the bounds: for them there is neither obligatory nor voluntary worship.
Madmen—yet the secret of their madness … is so exalted that reason prostrates at its gates.”

These are the words of a misguided man—indeed, a disbeliever—who imagines that a madman possesses a secret at whose threshold reason prostrates. This is because he has witnessed in some madmen a kind of disclosure of hidden matters or an astonishing feat beyond the ordinary. Such things occur because of the devils associated with the madman, just as they occur with sorcerers and soothsayers. This misguided man therefore imagines that anyone who discloses hidden matters or performs extraordinary feats is a friend of Allah.

Whoever believes this is a disbeliever by the consensus of Muslims, Jews, and Christians. For many disbelievers and polytheists, let alone the People of the Book, experience disclosures of hidden matters and extraordinary feats through their devils many times greater than those experienced by these people. The further a man strays and the greater his disbelief, the closer Satan is to him. Yet all these people’s disclosures necessarily contain lies and fabrications.

Their deeds must likewise involve wickedness and transgression, just as do those of their brethren among sorcerers and soothsayers. Allah Most High says:

“Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?”

“They descend upon every sinful liar.”

Thus, anyone upon whom the devils descend must be marked by lying

---

## Page 5026

and wickedness, whatever group he belongs to. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explained that Allah’s friends are those who draw near to Him through obligatory acts of worship: His successful party, His victorious army, and His righteous servants.

Whoever believes that someone who performs neither obligatory nor voluntary acts of worship—whether because he lacks reason, is ignorant, or for some other reason—is one of Allah’s pious friends; whoever regards such people as Allah’s pious friends, His successful party, and His righteous servants, is a disbeliever who has apostatized from the religion of the Lord of all worlds. If he says, “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,” he is among the liars of whom it is said:

“When the hypocrites come to you, they say, ‘We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.’ Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are certainly liars.”

“They have taken their oaths as a shield and have turned people away from the way of Allah. Evil indeed is what they have been doing.”

“That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, and they do not understand.”

It is authentically reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever neglects three Friday prayers out of carelessness, without an excuse, Allah will seal his heart.”

If the heart of someone who abandons Friday prayers is sealed even though he performs the noon prayer, what, then, of someone who performs neither the noon prayer nor the Friday prayer, neither obligatory nor voluntary prayers, and does not purify himself for prayer, whether by the full ritual bath or by ablution? Such a person, if he had previously been a believer and his heart had been sealed, would be a disbeliever and an apostate because of the obligations he abandoned and did not believe to be obligatory. If someone believes him to be a believer, that person is a disbeliever and an apostate. How, then, can he be considered one of the friends of

---

## Page 5027

Allah who are mindful of Him?

Allah Most High has said, describing the hypocrites:

“Satan has gained mastery over them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah.”

That is, he has taken control. The expression hādha al-ibila hawdhan means “he drove the camels along.” As for those over whom Satan has gained mastery, driving them to oppose what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, Allah Most High says:

“Do you not see that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers, inciting them relentlessly?”

That is, stirring them up violently. These are the people of whom He says:

“Satan has gained mastery over them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah. They are Satan’s party. Indeed, Satan’s party are the losers.”

In the Sunan collections, Abū al-Dardā’ reports that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whenever there are three people in a village among whom neither the call to prayer is made nor the prayer established, Satan gains mastery over them.”

Thus, any three of these people among whom neither the call to prayer is made nor the prayer established belong to Satan’s party, over whom he has gained mastery—not to the friends of the Most Merciful whom He has honoured. This remains so even if they are devoted worshippers and ascetics who practise hunger, sleeplessness, silence and seclusion, like the monks in monasteries and those who dwell in caves and caverns: the people of Mount Lebanon, Mount al-Fath at Asūn, Mount Laysūn, and the Cave of Blood on Mount Qāsiyūn, and other mountains and places frequented by many ignorant, misguided worshippers. There they undertake retreats and ascetic exercises without the call to prayer being made or the five daily prayers being established among them. Rather, they engage in acts of worship that neither Allah nor His Messenger has prescribed. They worship Him according to their own spiritual tastes and experiences, without assessing their states against the Quran and Sunnah

---

## Page 5028

or intending to follow the Messenger of Allah, concerning whom Allah said:

“Say, ‘If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins’”—to the end of the verse.

These people of religious innovation and misguidance belong to Satan’s party, not to the friends of the Most Merciful. Whoever testifies that they are friends of Allah is a lying, false witness who has strayed from the right path. Moreover, if he knows that these people oppose the Messenger, yet nevertheless testifies that they are friends of Allah, he is an apostate from Islam. He either rejects the Messenger as a liar, doubts and questions what he brought, or refuses to submit to him, opposing him instead out of denial, obstinacy, or obedience to his own desires. Every such person is a disbeliever.

If, however, he is ignorant of what the Messenger brought, while nevertheless believing that he is Allah’s Messenger to everyone in both inward and outward matters, and that there is no path to Allah except by following him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his case is different. He mistakenly supposes that these innovated acts of worship and satanic realities are among what the Messenger brought. He does not know that they come from Satan because he is ignorant of the Messenger’s Sunnah, law, approach, path, and the truth he brought—not because he intends to oppose him. Nor does he hope to find guidance anywhere other than in following him. The truth must be made clear to such a person, and he must be shown what the Sunnah and the Book say about his condition. If he repents and turns back to Allah, well and good; otherwise, he is classed with the preceding category and becomes a disbeliever and an apostate. Neither his worship nor his asceticism will save him from Allah’s punishment, just as these did not save the monks, the worshippers of crosses, the worshippers of fire, or the worshippers of idols, although many among them possess satanic supernatural powers and satanic unveilings. He said:

---

## Page 5029

exalted is He:

“Say, ‘Shall We inform you of those who lose most through their deeds? Those whose efforts have gone astray in this worldly life, while they think they are doing good.’”

Sa‘d ibn Abī Waqqās and others among the early generations said that this was revealed concerning those who inhabit hermitages and monasteries. It has also been reported from ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and others that they understood it to apply to the Harūriyyah and similar people of innovation and misguidance.

Allah, exalted is He, also said:

“Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every sinful liar.”

The liar is one who tells lies, and the sinner is a wicked person, as He said:

“We will surely seize him by the forelock—a lying, sinful forelock.”

Whoever speaks about religion without knowledge speaks falsely, even if he does not deliberately lie. This is established in the two Sahīh collections in a report from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Subay‘ah al-Aslamiyyah’s husband, Sa‘d ibn Khawlah, had died during the Farewell Pilgrimage while she was pregnant. She gave birth a few nights after her husband’s death, and Abū al-Sanābil ibn Ba‘kak told her, “You may not marry until the later of the two waiting periods has ended.” When she told the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said, “Abū al-Sanābil has spoken falsely. Rather, you are now free to marry, so marry.”

Likewise, when Salamah ibn al-Akwa‘ said, “They are saying that ‘Āmir killed himself and that his deeds have come to nothing,” he replied:

“Whoever said that has spoken falsely. He indeed strove earnestly and fought in Allah’s cause.”

The person who said this had not deliberately lied, for he was a righteous man. It has been reported that he was Usayd ibn al-Hudayr. Nevertheless, because he spoke without knowledge, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, declared that he had spoken falsely.

---

## Page 5030

Abū Bakr, Ibn Mas‘ūd, and other Companions also said concerning the rulings they issued through independent scholarly reasoning:

“If it is correct, it is from Allah; if it is mistaken, it is from me and from Satan, and Allah and His Messenger are free of it.”

If the error of a scholar exercising independent judgment, for which he is forgiven, is from Satan, what then of someone who speaks without the scholarly reasoning that would permit him to speak about religion? His error is likewise from Satan, but he will be punished for it unless he repents. The scholar’s error is from Satan, yet he is forgiven for it, just as wet dreams, forgetfulness, and other such things are from Satan and are forgiven. This is unlike someone who speaks without the scholarly reasoning that would permit him to do so: he speaks falsely and sins in this matter, even if he has good deeds in other matters.

Satan descends upon every person and inspires him in proportion to how much that person follows him, and is driven away in proportion to that person’s sincerity toward Allah and obedience to Him. Allah, exalted is He, said:

“Indeed, you have no authority over My servants.”

His servants are those who worship Him as His messengers commanded, performing obligatory and recommended deeds. As for someone who worships Him otherwise, he is one of Satan’s servants, not one of the servants of the Most Merciful.

Allah, exalted is He, said:

“Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan, for he is clearly your enemy, and that you should worship Me? This is a straight path. He has already led great multitudes of you astray. Did you not use your reason?”

Most of those who worship Satan do not realize that they are worshipping him. Rather, they may think that they are worshipping the angels or the righteous, like those who call upon them for help

---

## Page 5031

and prostrate before them. In reality, they have worshipped only Satan, even though they think they are seeking nearness to Allah and intercession through Allah’s righteous servants.

Allah, exalted is He, said:

“On the Day He gathers them all together, He will say to the angels, ‘Was it you these people used to worship?’”

“They will say, ‘Glory be to You! You are our Protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them believed in them.’”

For this reason, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade prayer at sunrise and sunset. Satan positions himself alongside the sun at those times so that the prostration of the sun-worshippers is directed to him. They think they are prostrating to the sun, whereas their prostration is to Satan.

The same applies to those who practise invocations of the heavenly bodies: they invoke a heavenly body, prostrate before it, address it privately, and call upon it. They prepare for it suitable food, clothing, incense, and means of seeking blessings, as described by the eastern author of al-Sirr al-maktūm (The Hidden Secret), by al-Būnī, the western author of al-Shuʿla al-nūrāniyya (The Luminous Flame), and by others. Spirits descend upon these people, speak to them, inform them of certain matters, and fulfil some of their needs. They call these the spirits of the heavenly bodies.

Some of them think that these are angels, whereas they are merely devils descending upon them. Allah, exalted is He, said:

“Whoever turns away from the Reminder of the Most Merciful, We assign to him a devil who becomes his companion.”

The Reminder of the Most Merciful is what He has sent down: the Book and the Sunnah, concerning which Allah said:

“Remember Allah’s favour upon you and what He has sent down to you of the Book and wisdom

---

## Page 5032

by which He admonishes you.” Allah, exalted is He, also said:

“Allah has certainly bestowed a great favour upon the believers by raising among them a Messenger from their own midst, reciting His verses to them, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom.”

And He, exalted is He, said:

“He is the One who raised among the unlettered people a Messenger from among themselves, reciting His verses to them, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom.”

This is the Reminder of which Allah said:

“Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and We will surely preserve it.”

Whoever turns away from this Reminder—the Book and the Sunnah—is assigned a devil as his companion and becomes one of Satan’s allies to the extent that he follows him. If he is loyal to the Most Merciful at times and to Satan at others, he possesses faith and friendship with Allah to the extent of his loyalty to the Most Merciful, and enmity towards Allah and hypocrisy to the extent of his loyalty to Satan.

As Hudhayfah ibn al-Yamān said, hearts are of “four kinds”: a pure heart containing a shining lamp—this is the believer’s heart; and a covered heart—this is the disbeliever’s heart. “Covered” means enclosed in a covering, as Allah, exalted is He, said concerning the Jews:

“And for their saying, ‘Our hearts are covered.’ Rather, Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief.”

The Prophet’s saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has already been cited:

“Whoever misses three Friday prayers, Allah seals his heart.”

Then there is an inverted heart—this is the hypocrite’s heart; and a heart with two sources of nourishment: one nourishing its faith and the other nourishing its hypocrisy. Whichever prevails determines its state.

This has also been narrated in the Musnad of Imām Ahmad as a report traced back to the Prophet. In the two Sahīh collections, ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘Ās reports from the Prophet

---

## Page 5033

may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“There are four traits: whoever possesses them is a complete hypocrite, and whoever possesses one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he abandons it: when entrusted, he betrays; when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a covenant, he breaks it; and when he disputes, he transgresses all bounds.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thus explained that the heart may contain both an element of hypocrisy and an element of faith. If it contains an element of hypocrisy, it contains a measure of friendship with Allah and a measure of enmity towards Him. Hence, extraordinary phenomena may occur through some of these people: those arising from their faith in Allah and their mindfulness of Him are miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s allies, while those arising from their hypocrisy and enmity towards Him are manifestations of devils.

For this reason, Allah, exalted is He, has commanded us to say in every prayer:

“Guide us to the straight path—the path of those You have blessed, not of those who have incurred Your wrath, nor of those who have gone astray.”

“Those who have incurred Your wrath” are those who know the truth but act contrary to it, while “those who have gone astray” are those who worship Allah without knowledge. Whoever follows his desires, his spiritual taste, and his inward experiences, knowing that he is acting contrary to the Book and the Sunnah, is among “those who have incurred Your wrath.” If he does not know this, he is among “those who have gone astray.”

We ask Allah to guide us to the straight path, the path of those He has blessed: the prophets, the steadfastly truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. What excellent companions they are! All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds. The final outcome belongs to the righteous. May Allah bless Muhammad.

---

## Page 5034

He was also asked:

“Is it correct to say, ‘The paths to Allah are as numerous as the breaths of created beings’?”

He replied:

If he means prescribed deeds that accord with the Book and the Sunnah—such as prayer, charity, jihad, remembrance of Allah, recitation, and the like—then this is correct. But if he means a path to Allah that conflicts with the Book and the Sunnah, then this is false. And Allah knows best.

---

## Page 5035

Shaykh al-Islām, the preeminent scholar of his age, Abū al-‘Abbās Ahmad ibn Taymiyyah—may Allah sanctify his soul and illuminate his grave—said:

All praise belongs to Allah. We praise Him, seek His help, guidance, and forgiveness, and seek refuge in Allah from the evils within ourselves and from our misdeeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray; and whomever He leads astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. May Allah bestow abundant blessings and peace upon him.

Shaykh Abū Muhammad ‘Abd al-Qādir said in the book Futūh al-Ghayb (Revelations of the Unseen):

“In all his circumstances, every believer must observe three things: a command to obey, a prohibition to heed, and a divine decree to accept with contentment.

---

## Page 5036

Thus, even in the simplest of circumstances, at least one of these three things applies to the believer. He should therefore bind his heart to them, remind himself of them, and govern his actions by them in all his circumstances.”

(I say): These are noble, comprehensive words that everyone needs. They set out in detail what the servant needs and accord with the saying of Allah Most High:

“Indeed, whoever fears Allah and is patient—Allah does not let the reward of those who do good go to waste.”

And His saying:

“If you are patient and fear Allah, their scheming will not harm you at all.”

And His saying:

“If you are patient and fear Allah, that is indeed a matter requiring firm resolve.”

“Fear of Allah” encompasses doing what is commanded and abstaining from what is forbidden, while “patience” encompasses patiently enduring what has been decreed. These “three things” thus come down to these two foundations. In reality, all three come down to obeying the command, which means obeying Allah and His Messenger.

The essence of the matter is that every servant needs, at every moment, to obey Allah and His Messenger: to do at that moment what he has been commanded to do at that moment. Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is the worship of Allah for which He created jinn and humankind. As He, Most High, says:

“I did not create jinn and humankind except to worship Me.”

And He, Most High, says:

“And worship your Lord until certainty comes to you.”

And He, Most High, says:

“O humankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, so that you may fear Him.”

---

## Page 5037

And all the messengers commanded their peoples to worship Allah and associate nothing with Him. Allah Most High says:

“We certainly sent a messenger to every nation, saying, ‘Worship Allah and shun false gods.’”

And He, Most High, says:

“Ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: Have We appointed gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?”

These “three things” come down to obeying the command because, when a person is commanded to perform an obligatory duty, such as the five daily prayers, Hajj, or the like, he needs to carry out that command. When circumstances conducive to sin arise, he needs to refrain from that sin, hate it, and restrain himself from committing it. This is doing what he has been commanded to do at that time. As for someone to whom the sin has never occurred, he has done nothing for which he is rewarded. Nevertheless, his not committing the sin necessarily means that he is safe from its punishment.

A mere absence that simply continues is not something one is commanded to bring about. Rather, a servant is commanded to do something within his power, and this must involve a new occurrence, whether bringing something into existence or causing something to cease to exist.

As for “the decree with which one is content,” when a person is afflicted with illness, poverty, or fear, he is commanded to be patient as an obligation. He is also commanded to be content, either as an obligation or as a recommendation; scholars of our school and others hold two views on this. Patience and contentment in the face of calamities are themselves obedience to Allah and His Messenger. They therefore fall under obeying the command and constitute worship of Allah.

---

## Page 5038

But although these “three things” fall under obeying the command when that expression is used without qualification, when they are distinguished and mentioned together, either they are singled out for explicit mention, or each expression is understood to convey something different from the other. This is exemplified by His words:

“So worship Him and put your trust in Him.”

And His words:

“So worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.”

These acts fall within worship when the term “worship” is used without qualification. When they are “mentioned together,” however, one may either say that the particular act is mentioned both generally and specifically, or that its specific mention makes it unnecessary to include it within the general term. Similar examples are His words, Most High:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.”

And His words:

“And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself wholly to Him. Lord of the East and the West—there is no deity except Him—so take Him as your Trustee. And be patient with what they say, and withdraw from them graciously.”

It may, however, be said that the expression “devoting oneself wholly” does not encompass these subsequent, conjoined commands in the way that the terms “worship” and “obedience” do.

“In sum,” there is a difference between what a person is commanded to do at the outset and what he is commanded to do when he needs to secure a benefit or ward off harm, or when he loves or hates something. The words of the shaykh—may Allah sanctify his soul—revolve around this central point: that one should do what is commanded, refrain from what is forbidden, and have no desire concerning anything beyond these two;

---

## Page 5039

so that he has no aim other than doing what Allah has commanded. As for what the servant has not been commanded to do, but which the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, brings about without the servant’s mediation, or brings about through him without any desire on his part, this is the divine decree with which he must be content. Later passages from the shaykh will clarify his intent and show that, in every circumstance, the servant must do what he has been commanded and refrain from what he has been forbidden.

But when He has not commanded the servant to do anything concerning the matter, we must submit to whatever the Lord brings about. This is the “reality” spoken of by the shaykh and others like him. To explain this reality in accordance with the revealed law, the matter falls into “two categories”:

(The first): The servant is commanded to respond to what the Lord has brought about, either by loving it and helping to bring it about, or by hating it and repelling it.

(The second): The servant is not commanded to do either.

(The first) includes, for example, righteousness and piety practised by someone else: the servant is commanded to love this and help that person in it. This includes helping those striving in Allah’s cause in their struggle, and helping all others who perform good deeds in their good works, as far as possible, while loving these deeds and being pleased with them. Likewise, when someone else suffers a calamity, the servant is commanded to act: by supporting someone who has been wronged, consoling someone afflicted by loss, relieving a poor person’s need, or doing something similar.

---

## Page 5040

As for what he is commanded to hate and repel, this includes cases where someone openly displays disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience. He is commanded to hate, repel, and denounce this as far as he is able, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said in the authentic hadith:

“Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand. If he cannot, then with his tongue. If he cannot, then with his heart—and that is the weakest level of faith.”

As for matters in which the servant is commanded to do neither, these include the permissible acts he sees another person performing, when it is not apparent to him that they are being used to assist in either obedience or sin. He is commanded neither to love nor to hate such acts. The same applies to his own purely permissible acts, which he does not intend to use to assist in either obedience or sin.

Yet this reflects a shortcoming on his part, for he ought to perform only those permissible acts that help him obey Allah, intending thereby to support his obedience. This is the path of the foremost, those brought near to Allah, who draw close to Allah Most High through voluntary acts of worship after fulfilling their obligations. Each of them continues drawing close to Him in this way until He loves him and becomes his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he grasps, and his foot with which he walks.

As for someone who performs permissible acts heedlessly, or engages in superfluous permissible activities that do not assist in obedience, while fulfilling his obligations and avoiding forbidden things both inwardly and outwardly, he is among those who follow a moderate course, the people of the right.

---

## Page 5041

And in short, actions that can fall under commands and prohibitions are not entirely neutral: if performed in a manner pleasing to Allah, doing them is better for the servant. Otherwise, refraining from them is better for him, even if he is not punished for doing them.

Superfluous permissible activities that do not assist in obedience are better left undone if, without them, he would occupy himself with obeying Allah, since they would distract him from that. If, however, they keep him occupied instead of something inferior, they are better for him than that inferior activity. If they keep him from disobeying Allah, they are a mercy for him, although occupying himself with obeying Allah is better for him than either.

The same applies to activities undertaken heedlessly or to satisfy desire that can help one obey Allah: sleep intended to support worship, and eating, drinking, clothing, and marriage, which can likewise support worship. If the servant does not have that intention, this is a shortcoming on his part and a missed opportunity for a good deed and something good that Allah loves. It is recorded in the two Sahīhs that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Saʿd:

“You will never spend anything seeking Allah’s pleasure without thereby rising in degree and rank—even the morsel you place in your wife’s mouth.”

It is also recorded in the Sahīh that he said:

“When a Muslim spends on his family seeking Allah’s reward, it is charity.”

Thus, permissible activities that one does not need, or that one needs but undertakes without the faith that would make them a good deed, are better left undone if, without them, one would occupy oneself with what is

---

## Page 5042

better than them. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“When one of you has sexual intercourse, it is charity.” They asked, “O Messenger of Allah, does one of us satisfy his desire and receive a reward for it?” He replied, “If he were to satisfy it unlawfully, would he not incur sin?” They said, “Yes.” He said, “Likewise, when he satisfies it lawfully, he receives a reward for it. Why, then, do you take account of the unlawful but not the lawful?”

This is because, when a believer feels sexual desire, he intends to turn away from what Allah has forbidden towards what Allah has permitted. He intends to do what is permissible, believing that Allah has permitted it.

“Allah loves His concessions to be taken, just as He hates acts of disobedience to be committed against Him.”

This was narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad and by others. For this reason, Allah loves the use of the concessions of shortening the prayer and not fasting. Thus, when a believer turns away from monasticism, excessive strictness, and self-torment—which Allah does not love—and instead avails himself of the concessions Allah loves, this is among the good deeds for which Allah rewards him. This is so even though the act itself is permissible, because of the belief and intention accompanying it, both of which constitute obedience to Allah and His Messenger. Actions are judged only by intentions, and each person will have only what he intended.

Furthermore, the servant is commanded to engage in those permissible activities that he needs: he is commanded to eat when hungry and drink when thirsty. Hence, someone compelled by necessity to eat carrion must eat it. If he refused to eat until he died, he would deserve the threatened punishment. This is the position of the vast majority of scholars, including the four imams and others. Likewise, he is commanded to have intercourse when he needs it; indeed, he is even commanded

---

## Page 5043

to enter into the marriage contract itself when he needs it and is able to do so. As for the statement of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, “When one of you has sexual intercourse, it is charity,” intercourse is prescribed to meet both his need and the woman’s need. Meeting her need—which can only be satisfied through him—in a lawful manner is charity.

Spiritual wayfaring takes two forms: the way of the righteous, the people of the right, which consists of fulfilling obligations and avoiding forbidden things, inwardly and outwardly; and (the second), the way of those brought near to Allah, the foremost, which consists of doing what is obligatory and recommended as far as possible, and avoiding what is disliked and forbidden. As the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“When I forbid you something, avoid it; and when I command you to do something, do as much of it as you can.”

The words of the great spiritual masters, such as Shaykh ‘Abd al-Qādir and others, point to this way. Hence, they enjoin what is recommended but not obligatory, and forbid what is disliked but not prohibited. They guide the elite along the path of the elite, and ordinary people along the path of ordinary people. The path of the elite is the path of those brought near to Allah: that the servant should do only what he has been commanded to do, and desire only what Allah and His Messenger have commanded him to desire—namely, what is loved by

---

## Page 5044

Allah, approved by Him, and willed by Him in the religious, legislative sense. Otherwise, all events are willed by Him in the sense that He creates them and brings them into being.

Unconditional acquiescence in His creative, decretive will is neither rationally possible nor prescribed by divine law. This is because some events must be prevented and may not be desired. For example, someone may seek to bring a man or his family into disbelief, commit sexual immorality with him or his family, kill the Prophet when one is able to prevent it, or lead people astray and corrupt their religious and worldly affairs. Such things must be resisted and hated; it is not permissible to desire them.

As for its rational impossibility, human beings are naturally disposed to love what suits them and hate what is repugnant to them. When hungry, a person loves what satisfies his hunger, such as food, and does not love what fails to satisfy it, such as earth. His desire for these two things cannot possibly be equal. Likewise, he loves faith and righteous deeds, which benefit him, and hates disbelief and wickedness, which harm him. Indeed, he loves Allah and worshipping Him alone, and hates worshipping anything besides Him.

As Abraham, Allah’s close friend, said:

“Have you considered what you have been worshipping—you and your forefathers? They are enemies to me, except the Lord of all worlds.”

And Allah Most High said:

“You have an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, ‘We disown you and whatever you worship besides Allah. We reject you, and enmity and hatred have arisen between us and you forever, until

---

## Page 5045

you believe in Allah alone.’”

Allah has commanded us to follow the example of Abraham and those with him when they disowned the polytheists and whatever they worshipped besides Allah. Allah’s close friend said:

“I disown whatever you worship, except the One who created me, for He will surely guide me.”

Disavowal is the opposite of allegiance: disavowal is rooted in hatred, while allegiance is rooted in love. This is because the essence of affirming Allah’s oneness is to love none but Allah, and to love what Allah loves for His sake. Thus, one loves only for Allah’s sake and hates only for Allah’s sake.

Allah Most High said:

“Yet among people are those who take others as equals to Allah, loving them as they love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah.”

There is a clear distinction between loving for Allah’s sake and loving alongside Allah. Those who affirm Allah’s oneness and devote themselves sincerely to Him love others for Allah’s sake, whereas the polytheists love others alongside Allah—as the polytheists love their gods, the Christians love the Messiah, and the followers of their own desires love their leaders.

Once it is understood that the servant is naturally disposed to love what benefits him and hate what harms him, it follows that, by his very nature and constitution, he cannot desire all events equally. Nor does divine law command him to desire everything that happens. Rather, Allah has commanded him to desire certain things and dislike others.

---

## Page 5046

The Messengers—may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them—were sent to perfect and affirm the natural disposition, not to transform or change it. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Every child is born upon the natural disposition; then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian.”

Allah Most High said:

“So set your face towards the religion, inclining to pure faith—the natural disposition Allah instilled in mankind. There is no altering Allah’s creation. That is the upright religion, but most people do not know.”

An authentic hadith reports that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah Most High says: ‘I created My servants devoted to Me alone, but the devils led them astray, forbade them what I had made lawful for them, and commanded them to associate with Me that for which I had sent down no authority.’”

The upright faith consists in steadfastly devoting one’s religion sincerely to Allah. This entails loving Him Most High and humbling oneself before Him, associating nothing with Him in either love or submission. Worship combines the utmost love with the utmost humility, and none but Allah alone deserves this. Likewise, one must hold Allah alone in awe, be mindful of Him alone, and place one’s trust in Him alone.

The Messenger is to be obeyed and loved: lawful is what he has declared lawful, forbidden is what he has forbidden, and religion is what he has prescribed.

Allah Most High said:

“Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, fears Allah and is mindful of Him—it is they who will triumph.”

Allah Most High also said:

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger. To Allah alone we turn with hope.’”

---

## Page 5047

And this is the essence of the religion of Islam. The Messengers were sent with this, as Allah Most High said:

“He has ordained for you the religion He enjoined upon Noah, that which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: uphold the religion and do not become divided over it.”

Allah Most High also said:

“O Messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds. Indeed, I know all that you do.”

“And indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so be mindful of Me.”

This, then, is the foundation to which everyone must hold firmly. Each person must desire and love what Allah has commanded them to desire and love, and dislike and hate what Allah has commanded them to dislike and hate.

In this regard, people fall into “four categories”: the most perfect are those who love what Allah and His Messenger love and hate what Allah and His Messenger hate. They desire what Allah and His Messenger have commanded them to desire, and dislike what Allah and His Messenger have commanded them to dislike. They have no love or hatred beyond that. They enjoin what Allah and His Messenger have enjoined, and nothing else; they forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and nothing else.

Such is the state of the two intimate friends of Allah, the best of creation: Muhammad and Abraham, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace. And indeed,

---

## Page 5048

it is authentically reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah has taken me as an intimate friend, just as He took Abraham as an intimate friend.”

He also said in an authentic hadith:

“By Allah, I do not give to anyone or withhold from anyone; I am only a distributor, allocating as I am commanded.”

He mentioned that his Lord gave him the choice between being a prophet-king and being a servant-messenger, and he chose to be a servant-messenger. A “prophet-king” is like David and Solomon. Allah Most High said:

“This is Our gift, so give or withhold, without account.”

They explained its meaning as follows: “Give to whomever you wish and withhold from whomever you wish; We will not call you to account.” Thus, a “prophet-king” gives according to his own will and is not punished for doing so, just as someone freely chooses to do permissible things. The “servant-messenger,” however, neither gives nor withholds except by his Lord’s command—that is, in accordance with His love, His pleasure, and His prescriptive will. Those who are foremost and brought near to Allah are followers of the servant-messenger, while those who take a middle course, the people of the right, are followers of the prophet-king.

A person may also be in a state devoid of either kind of intention: he has no intention concerning giving or withholding—neither a religious intention that he is commanded to have, nor a personal desire, whether forbidden or not. Rather, whatever happens is what he wills, and whatever is done to him is what he wills, without his doing what religious law commands in that situation.

---

## Page 5049

Such a person is like someone who has wealth to give away but has no particular intention governing his giving—neither an intention prescribed by religious law nor a blameworthy one. Rather, he gives to everyone. Assuming that he has fulfilled his obligations to the best of his ability, but Allah’s prescriptive will concerning the details of his actions remains unclear to him, he is not blamed for what he does, nor is he praised without qualification. Rather, he is praised for being free of personal desire. Had he known the details of what he was commanded to do and intended to act accordingly, his state would have been more perfect. Indeed, when one is able, doing so is either obligatory or recommended.

His state is better than that of someone whose choices are governed by his own desires and inclinations, even when those choices are permissible. Yet he falls short of someone whose choices are governed by his Lord’s command, rather than by personal desire or divine decree alone.

In sum, with regard to permissible matters such as authority, wealth, and the like, people fall into “three categories”:

Some act in these matters only according to the commands of religious law. This is the state of our Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: the state of the servant-messenger and those who follow him in this respect.

Others act in these matters according to their own wishes and desires that are not forbidden. This is the state of the prophet-king, and the state of the righteous, the people of the right.

Still others act according to neither of these. As for “the former,” this is due to their lack of

---

## Page 5050

knowledge of it. As for “the latter,” this is due to their detachment from it. Rather, they act in these matters according to divine decree alone, following Allah’s will as expressed in creation and decree when knowledge of His prescriptive will and commands is unattainable. This is like deciding by drawing lots when no known basis in religious law allows one option to be preferred over another. In this state, they may act upon inspiration that arises in their hearts and words addressed to them.

The words of “Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir”—may Allah sanctify his soul—often concern this state. He enjoins detachment from the self’s will and desires, so that a person no longer acts at their bidding. This raises him above the state of the righteous, the people of the right, and above the way of kings altogether. Whoever attains this and acts according to the religious commands conveyed by Muhammad and set out in the Quran is the most perfect of people. Yet these commands may be unclear to him, for knowing them in detail may be impossible or difficult in many situations.

Do you not see that when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, appointed Saʿd ibn Muʿādh to judge Banū Qurayzah, and he ruled that their fighting men should be killed, their offspring taken captive, and their property taken as spoils, he said:

“You have indeed judged them according to Allah’s judgment from above the seven heavens.”

This is because the ruler’s choice between execution, enslavement, release without ransom, and ransom is not a choice governed by personal desire, but one governed by sound judgment and the common good. He must therefore choose what best serves that good. If he chooses this, he has accorded with Allah’s judgment; otherwise, he has not. Since this is often unclear, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in the hadith

---

## Page 5051

which is authentic:

“If you besiege the people of a fortress and they ask you to accept their surrender subject to Allah’s judgment, do not accept their surrender subject to Allah’s judgment, for you do not know what Allah’s judgment concerning them is. Rather, accept their surrender subject to your judgment and that of your companions.”

The ruler who accepts the surrender of a fortress’s inhabitants subject to his judgment must rule according to his independent legal judgment. Thus, when he instructed Saʿd to adopt the course most pleasing and beloved to Allah, Saʿd ruled in accordance with His judgment. Had he ruled otherwise, his ruling would still have been binding, since he had exercised his independent legal judgment, even if it did not accord with Allah’s actual judgment.

In circumstances like these, where the religious command concerning a particular case is unclear, Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir and other shaykhs like him advise “at times” turning to inward prompting and inspiration, if possible, and “at other times” relying on divine decree alone, because no grounds supplied by religious law are available for preferring one course over another—just as the Lawgiver provides for choosing by lot. They instruct a person not to prefer one course merely on the basis of his own will and desire, since this is either forbidden, disliked, or diminishes his merit. Their prohibition here resembles their prohibition of excessive indulgence in permissible things.

Then, if the religious command becomes clear to them, they must base their choice upon it. Otherwise, they choose either on the basis of “an inward cause,” such as inspiration and inward perception, or through “divine ordainment and decree,” which are not attributable to them. Whoever, in such circumstances, chooses by “seeking Allah’s guidance”—just as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to teach his Companions to seek Allah’s guidance in all matters, as he taught them a surah of the Quran—has acted correctly.

---

## Page 5052

This is analogous to the case in which the evidence concerning a “question of religious law” appears conflicting to a jurist exercising independent legal judgment or to a follower seeking a legal ruling: they do not give preference to either position. Rather, they accept whatever divine decree brings about and do not object to it.

At other times, one of them gives preference to a course of action on the basis of a dream, the opinion of a sincere adviser, or a benefit he perceives in one of the two courses.
